KBGN -0023 and KBGN-0073 both dated 25-2-74 of the defendant No. 1 who carries on shipping business at the port of Chittagong through their local agent, the defendant No. 2. The carrying vessel arrived at the port of Chittagong on or about 18-3-1974 and discharged her cargoes on subsequent dates at the Chittagong port jetties belonging to the defendant No. 3. Then, the plaintiff is exempted from payment of customs duty and sales tax for importing of fishing materials which include nylon twine and accordingly after obtaining the exemption certificate, the plaintiff handed over the documents to the defendant No. 5 who was appointed as clearing agent, for the purpose of clearance of the goods from the port of Chittagong. Then, the defendant No. 5 after observing formalities obtained delivery orders for the suit consignments from the defendant No. 2 as the local agent of the defendant No. 1. Then, after taking delivery orders from the defendant No. 2, when the defendant No. 5 went to take delivery of the goods a large number of cartons of both the consignments were found in damaged condition. Then, the defendant No. 5 filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons before taking delivery of the same from the port of Chittagong, but the defendant No. 2 refused the joint survey. The defendant No. 5, therefore, got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyors. As per survey report being No. MSR/CTC/00-107/ 74 out of the surveyed 160 cartons of the consignment of 396, there was shortage of 3708 lbs and as per survey report No. MSR/CTG /00-106/ 74, out of the surveyed 200 cartons of the consignment of 614 cartons, there was shortage of 4707 lbs. That the surveyor attributed the cause of shortage to be due to pilferage/theft during transit and as a result of such shortage the plaintiff suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22 as per Schedule of the claim. It was further case of the plaintiff that the suit consignments were insured with the defendant No. 4, the Sadharan Bima Corporation, under Policy No. CTG-A /M/P/206/3 /74 and No. CTG/A/M/P/205/3/74 respectively. Accordingly, the plaintiff lodged claims with the defendants who did not settle the claim and, as such, the plaintiff was constrained to file the instant suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 jointly and 3, 4, and 5 individually appeared in the suit by filing separate written statements denying the plaintiffs' claim and material allegations. Subsequently, all these defendants contested the suit except the defendant No. 5.

4. The case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, in short, is that the suit vessel arrived at the port of Chittagong on 18-3-74 and discharged the consignment on 18-3-74 and 19-3-74 into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3 and the said vessel sailed from Chittagong port after completing her discharge of the cargoes on 28-3-74. It was further contended that some cartons landed with trivial damage which was nominal and of trivial nature due to normal handling and the landing position was fully known to the plaintiff and their clearing agent. The plaintiff and their clearing agent acted negligently and carelessly in not arranging for delivery of the goods in time which resulted in theft and pilferage while the goods were lying in custody of the defendant No. 3 after discharge from the vessel and, as such, this defendant is not liable for the alleged loss. Therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost as against this defendant.

5. The case of the defendant No. 3, in short, is that the goods landed in damaged condition from the vessel, apparent condition being noted as torn in joint tally and delivered to the plaintiffs clearing agent in the same condition as received. Therefore, the plaintiffs clearing agent failed to clear the goods within five days from the actual date of landing as required under section 50B(2) of the Port Act and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed as against this defendant with cost.

6. The case of the defendant No. 4, in short, is that the goods in suit were landed from the carrying ship into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3 on 18-3-74 under qualified remarks. The policies were taken on 21-3-74 subsequent to the date of landing of the goods and subsequent to the alleged damage of the goods. The alleged loss of the plaintiff is not therefore, covered by the policy issued by the defendant No. 4 who is not liable for any part of the claim in the suit and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs as against this defendant.

7. Plaintiff examined only one witness as PW 1 and produced number of documents, which were marked, exhibit. while the defendants examined none but produced number of documents, which were also marked as exhibit.

8. Trial Court on considering the facts and circumstance, evidence on record and other allied legal aspects decreed the suit on contest against the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 only and dismissed against the rest directing the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to pay the decretal amount of Taka 89,693.22 to the plaintiff within thirty days together with cost and interest @ 10% per annum with effect from the date of filing the suit till realisation. Hence, the appeal.

9. Mr Md Ohiullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that the learned trial Court erred in law in passing the decree against the defendants/appellants although the suit against the defendants/ Appellants is barred by limitation. The trial Court erred in law in not holding that this Court has no jurisdiction to try and entertain the suit in view of the jurisdiction clause contained in the Bill of Lading and erred in law in not holding that the defendants/appellants could not be held liable for shortage of goods since the consignment were discharged into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3 and the vessel sailed from Chittagong Port after completing the discharge of the suit consignment.

10. He further submits that the trial Court erred in law in not holding that the plaintiff and their agent acted negligently and carelessly in not arranging for delivery of the goods in time which resulted in theft and pilferage while the goods were lying in custody of the defendant No. 3.

11. He lastly submits that the trial Court erred in law in not holding that since the cargo were discharged from the vessels 'MV Victoria Peak' under qualified marks into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3, the defendants /Appellants are not liable to pay any compensation as claimed by the plaintiff and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

12. He finally drew the attention of the court and submits that the trial Court erred in law in relying on the finding of survey report, which was conducted unilaterally long after four months from the date of discharge of the cargo and, as such, the judgment of the learned trial Court is otherwise bad in law and erroneous and liable to be set aside and the suit should be dismissed against the defendants/ Appellants.

13. The plaintiff No. 1 submits that the defendant No. 5 as a clearing agent of plaintiff No. 1 after taking delivery order when went to take delivery of the goods, a large number of cartons of both consignments were found in damaged conditions and, as such, defendant No. 5, filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons before taking delivery of the same. But the defendant No. 2 refused the joint survey on baseless grounds and on refusal of the joint survey, the defendant No. 5 got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyor, which reports that there was shortage of cartons caused due to pilferage/ theft during transit and, as such, the plaintiff suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22 and upon considering such report the trial Court rightly decreed the suit.

14. Defendant No. 2 is the agent of defendant No. 1 and, as such, agent gave a declaration under section 55(e) of the Customs Act, 1969 undertaking to discharge all claims for damage /or shortage of goods comprised in ship's Import General Manifest. The defendant No. 2 has therefore, incurred an independent statutory liability and is liable for the claim of the plaintiff.

15. We have perused the records along with the judgment and decree and heard the learned Advocates.

16. Facts stated herein above need not be reiterated. Only question that is facing us is, whether the trial Court is well justified in decreeing the suit.

17. The plaintiff on 17-3-75 instituted the suit for realisation of Taka 89,693.22 against the defendants as compensation as per report of the surveyor. In course of its business, the plaintiff imported two consignments of Nylon Twine consisting of 614 and 396 cartons from Japan covered by bill of lading dated 25-2-74 by defendant No. 1 who is carrying on shipping business at the Chittagong Port through its local agent, the defendant No. 2. The carrying vessel arrived at the Port of Chittagong on or about 18-3-74 and discharged her cargo on subsequent dates thereon belonging to the defendant No. 3. After completion of all formalities, the plaintiff handed over the documents to defendant No. 5, who was appointed as Clearing Agent, for the purpose of clearance of the goods imported. The defendant No. 5 after observing other formalities obtained delivery orders for the suit consignment from the defendant No. 2 as agent of defendant No. 1 and when he went to take delivery of the goods, a large number of cartons of both the consignment were found in damaged condition. As a result, defendant No. 5 filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons but defendant No. 2 refused it. Then, defendant No. 5 got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyors, which gave report that there was total shortage of (4707 + 3708) = 8415 lbs out of two consignments. It also attributed that the cause of shortage to be pilferage/theft during transit and, as such, the plaintiff has suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22.

<u>18. It is admitted that the vessel arrived on 18-3-74 and discharged it cargoes on 18-3-74 and 19-3-74 into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3. Some cartons landed with trivial damages, which was nominal and of trivial nature due to normal handling and landing which was fully known to the plaintiff and after completion of discharge, the said vessel sailed out from Chittagong port on 28-3-74. It is also admitted that the defendant No. 5 as clearing agent of the plaintiff did not take any step for delivery of the consignments from the defendant No. 2, local agent of defendant No. 1 within stipulated period of time i.e. five days under section 50B(2) of the Chittagong Port Act. The plaintiff handed over documents to his clearing agent, defendant No. 5, for the purpose of clearance of the goods from the Chittagong Port on 2-6-74 and said clearing agent approached the defendant No. 3 for obtaining delivery of the suit consignment after a lapse of about four months. Moreover, the plaintiff or his clearing agent, the defendant No. 5 did not take any steps to get the alleged damaged goods surveyed before 29-7-74 though they knew that some cartons landed with trivial damage, which was nominal and of trivial nature due to normal handling. Trial Court only considering the report of surveyors surveyed on behalf of the plaintiff decreed the suit against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 only, which cannot be sustained in law. Moreover, we also perused the cross-examination of PW-1, Delowar Hossain Siddique who deposed only on behalf of plaintiff. In his cross-examination, he admitted that he does not have any personal knowledge about the importation of the suit consignment; that he did not know whether 268 cartons of goods had landed from the vessel and recorded with the marks 'T' vide tally sheets was not within his knowledge; that he could not recollect whether he had appointed the defendant No. 5 as the clearing agent of the plaintiff; that he was not aware on what date the delivery order was received by the defendant No. 5 from the defendant No. 2; that he could not say when was the letter written to the defendant No. 2 for joint survey; that he was not present during the time of survey. After such cross-examination how the trial Court opined that the plaintiff successfully proved its case is not understood. Even, the plaintiff did not take any step to examine the surveyor.</u>

19. In view of the above discussions, we find substance in the appeal.

20. In the result, the appeal is allowed. Impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court is hereby set aside and the suit is dismissed, without any order as to costs.

Send down the lower court's records.

End.
