full_judgment:
Gobinda Chandra Tagore J: This Rule Nisi obtained under Article 102 (1) read with Article 44 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calls upon the respondents to show cause as to why the provision of Rule 11(3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 (Annexure-D) should not be declared ultra virus the Articles 27, 29, and 31 of the Constitution and why the action of respondent Nos. 1-3 in issuing Memo No. C Bari/Uma-115/93/Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-R) by respondent No. 3, pursuant to the decision of the respondent No. .1 contained in letter No. Sal-AT-Opinion-31/2006/ 579 dated 23-7-2006, issued under the signature of respondent No. 2 appointing an Inquiry Officer for holding re-inquiry in the depart-mental proceeding No. 1 of 1993 against the petitioner under Rule 11 (3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985, should not be declared illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional, violative of the petitioner's fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution and to have been taken without lawful authority and why the respondents should not be directed to reinstate the petitioner in service as per the direction of the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal and/or such other or further-order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Shortly the relevant facts necessary for disposal of the Rule Nisi are:

The petitioner was appointed as peon by respondent No. 3 and he joined the service on 1-11-1976. He worked in different sections of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal to the full satisfaction of the superior officers. He was transferred to the Court of Magistrate, Hijla in 1986. When he was serving in the Court of Magistrate, Hijla, he was promoted to the post of process server in 1988. Thereafter, he was transferred to the office of the Thana Nirbahi Officer, Ujirpur in 1989. Then by letter No. 102(6) Nezarat dated 23-2-1993, he was posted to work on deputation at the Bungalow of the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal with the direction to resume his duty on 23-2-1993 and accordingly, he resumed his duty. But he was again transferred by the Nezarat, Deputy Collect orate, Barisal to the Court of Thana Magistrate, Ujirpur by letter No. 123 (28)/ Nezarat dated 6-3-1993. The order of transfer doted 6-3-1993 was cancelled by the Nezarat vide letter No. 137 (6) Nezarat dated 17-3-1993. Accordingly, he was working in the Bungalow of the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal. The order of deputation was never withdrawn nor was the petitioner ever directed to work at the Office of Thana Nirbahi Officer, Ujirpur. Subsequently, the petitioner went to the office of the Thana Nirbahi Officer to resume his duty on 27-3-1993, but he was not allowed to work there. The petitioner was suspended from service on 30-6-1993 on the ground of misconduct and desertion till initiation of and pending the departmental proceeding against him. A departmental proceeding was drawn up against the petitioner being Departmental Proceeding Case No. 1 of 1993 and charge was framed against him by an order dated 30-6-1.993 under Rule 3 (b) and (c) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1985 and he was asked to show cause as to why he should not be dismissed/removed from service or suitably punished otherwise. The petitioner on receipt of the charges submitted his written defense to respondent. No. 3 denying the allegations made in the charge sheet.

3. Thereafter, on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal Mr Md Mohibul Haque, Nezarat, Deputy Collectorate, Barisal on 14-8-1993 appointed Sayeda A froz Begum, Assistant Commissioner, Barisal Collectorate, as Inquiry Officer for holding inquiry into the charge against the petitioner. The Inquiry Officer by an order dated 16-8-1993 issued a notice of inquiry fixing 23-8-1993 for hearing and directing the petitioner to be present in her office. The petitioner appeared before the Inquiry Officer on 23-8-1993. The Inquiry Officer recorded the statement of the petitioner and she herself put different questions to and cross examined him. The Inquiry Officer herself examined 4 persons at a time in her room, but the petitioner was not allowed to cross examine them during the inquiry and thus he was denied reasonable opportunity or defense at the inquiry. The charge brought against the petitioner was not proved and established by any legal evidence. The Inquiry Officer acted as the prosecutor and the Judge at the same time. The whole inquiry was vitiated for non-compliance with the pro-vision of Rule 10 of the Rules, 1985 and the Principle of Natural Justice. On receipt of the inquiry report, respondent No. 3 by his order dated 28-10-1993 issued second show cause notice, but the petitioner was not supplied with the copy of the inquiry report as required under Rule 7 (5) of the Rules, 1985. The petitioner submitted his reply to the second show cause notice to respondent No. 3 denying the allegations made therein. Respondent No. 3 by his order dated 26-12-1993 confirmed the punishment of dismissal from service already proposed in the second show cause notice. The petitioner preferred departmental appeal to the appellate authority on 9-2-1994, which was dismissed by an order dated 27-2-1996.

4. Then the petitioner filed Administrative Tribunal Case No. 73 of 1996 on 24-4-1996 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka challenging the legality of the order of dismissal dated 26-12-1993 and the order dated 27-2-1996 dismissing the appeal by the appellate authority and for a direction upon the respondents to reinstate him in service with all attendant financial benefits as admissible under the Rules. Subsequently, the Administrative Tribunal Case No. 73 of 1996 was transferred to the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal and it was renumbered as Administrative Tribunal Case No. 19 of 2002. Respondent No. 3 con-tested the case by filing written statement denying the allegations made in the application. It was contended before the Administrative Tribunal that the whole proceeding has been vitiated for non-compliance with the mandatory provisions of Rule 7(5) and 10(2) and 10(4) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and the Principle of Natural Justice.

5. The learned Member of the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal disposed of the case upon consideration of the facts and circumstances and the materials on record as well as the provisions of law. By the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002, the Administrative Tribunal was pleased to allow the case and declared the order of dismissal dated 26-12-1993 passed by Respondent No. 3 and the order dated 27-2-1996 passed by the Appellate Authority dismissing the departmental appeal as illegal, inoperative and void with a direction on the authorities to reinstate the petitioner in service. Thereafter on 12-5-2003 the petitioner submitted his joining report to the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal (Respondent No. 3) along with a copy of the judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal. The petitioner persuaded the matter to the authority, but no action was taken. The respondents did not prefer any appeal against the judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal. Batter long lapse of about 4 years, ignoring the directions of the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal, passed in its judgment and order dated  11-9-2002 for reinstatement of the petitioner in service, respondent' No. 3 issued impugned Memo DC: Bari/Uma415/93/Nirzarat-541 dated 28-8-2006, Annexure-B with reference to impugned vide Memo No. Sal/AT/Opinion-31 /2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 issued under the signature of respondent No. 2 appointing Ni Md Muklesur Rahman Ahmad, Assistant Com-missioner and Magistrate, Collectorate, Barisal as inquiry Officer for holding 're-inquiry' in the departmental proceeding No. 1 of 1993 under Rule 11 (3) Of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. A copy of the impugned Memo was served on the petitioner. But no copy of impugned Memo No Sal /AT/ Opinion-3/2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 was given to the petitioner. However, the petitioner procured a copy of the same, which runs as under:—

ত্রুটি ও তামাদির কারণে আপীল অগ্রাহ্য হওয়ার আশংকা থাকায় এবং অন্যদিকে অপরাধ গুরুতর হওয়ায় ও পুনঃ তদন্ত করার সুযোগ সরকারী কর্মচারী (শৃংখলা ও আপীল) বিধিমালা, ১৯৮৫ এর বিধি ১১(৩) এ বিদ্যমান থাকায় পুনঃ তদন্ত করার শর্তে আপীল দায়ের না করার সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করা হইল ৷

6. Pursuant to impugned Memo No. DC: Bari/Uma-115/93 Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-B), the Inquiry Officer issued notice vide Memo No. DC: Bari/B: B/132 dated 11-9-2006, Annexure-C fixing 21-9-2006 for holding re-inquiry and asking the petitioner to be present there with necessary papers.

7. Being aggrieved by the provision of Rule 11 (3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1985 (Annexure-D) by the decision contained in letter No. Sal-AT-Opinion-31/2006/579 dated 23-7-2006 to hold 're-inquiry' there under in Departmental Proceeding No. 1 of 1993 against the petitioner and by Memo No. DC: Bari/Uma-115/93/ Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-B) issued appointing an inquiry officer in this regard, the petitioner filed the writ petition and obtained the Rule Nisi.

8. Mr SAM Mahbub Elahi along with Mr Md Zahurul Alam and Mr Eaqub Ali Hawlader, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned Rule 11. (3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and. Appeal) Rules, 1985 is unconstitutional and violative of Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution because it having not provided for any guide-lines or principles, it confers absolute and unfettered discretion to the concerned authority in directing a further enquiry against a Government servant on the same allegation after the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service imposed upon him by the authority on the allegation is set aside, or declared or rendered void in consequence of or by a decision of a Court of Law of Administrative Tribunal.

9. Having relied upon the case of Dr Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201, he further submits that the impugned Rule 11 (3) does not provide any guidelines or principles for exercise of the discretion of the concerned authority and consequently such absolute and unfettered discretion may be exercised on pick and choose basis discriminating against the public servants similarly placed and such discrimination is inherent in the impugned Rule 11 (3) itself and, as such, the same being violative of Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution is ultra vires the Constitution.

10. Again referring the same case of Dr Nuul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201, he submits that the respondents neither took any steps under the impugned Rule 11(3) nor had they preferred any appeal against the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 of the Administrative Tribunal within the statutory period of limitation, but long after about 4 (four) years they resorted to the impugned Rule 11 (3) in o mala fide intention to harass and humiliate the petitioner and, as such, impugned Memo Nos. Sal-AT-Opinion-31 / 2006/579 dated 23-7-2006 and DC: Bari/Uma-115/93/Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-B) are liable to be declared to have been issued out of malice both in law and fact, without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

11. Mr Karunamaya Chakma, learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the Rule Nisi is not maintainable as the petitioner had alternative efficacious remedy in the Administrative Tribunal.

12. In reply, the learned Advocate submits that the writ petition has been filed challenging the constitutionality of the impugned Rule 11(3) and the writ petition involves interpretation of Rule 11(3) as to whether it confers any unfettered and absolute discretion to the concerned authority to conduct any further or re-inquiry against any Government servant on the same allegation at anytime, whenever they wish or even after expiry of the statutory period of limitation for preferring any appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal or any Appellate Court of law against the judgment and order of Administrative Tribunal or of a Court of law setting aside the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service on the allegation and, as such, the writ petition is quite maintainable.

13. We have perused the writ petition and the annexure thereto and heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the learned Deputy attorney General as well.

14. It is an admitted fact that upon contesting hearing Administrative Tribunal, Barisal allowed Administrative Tribunal Case No. 19 of 2002 by the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 declaring the order of dismissal dated 26-12-1993 passed by Respondent No. 3 and the order dated 27-2-1996 passed by the Appellate Attorney dismissing the departmental appeal as illegal, inoperative and void with a direction on the authorities to reinstate the petitioner in service.

15. It has also not been controverter that on 12-5-2003 the petitioner submitted his joining report to the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal, respondent No. 3 along with a copy of the judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal. The petitioner persuaded the matter to the respondents, but they did not take any action nor had they preferred any appeal against the judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal. Then one after another about 4 years elapsed, but the respondents did not comply with the direction of the Administrative Tribunal to reinstate the petitioner in his service. Only on 28-8-2006, respondent No. 3 issued impugned Memo No. DC: Bari /Uma-115/93/Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006, Annexure-B with reference to impugned Memo No. Sal/AT/Opinion-31 /2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 issued under the signature of respondent No. 2 appointing Mr Md Muklesur Rahman Akand, Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate, Collectorate, Barisal as Inquiry Officer for holding 're-inquiry' in the departmental proceeding No. 1 of 1993 under the impugned Rule]] (3) of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985.

16. It appears from impugned Memo No. Sal/AT/Opinion-31 /2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 quoted before that as there was procedural defect in the departmental proceedings and as the appeal being barred by limitation it might be rejected, it was decided not to prefer any appeal on the condition of holding 're-inquiry' under Rule 11 (3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 in the departmental proceedings against the petitioner.

17. The Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 was made by respondent No. 4 vide Notification No. SRO 381L/85/ ME(R-V) ID-13/84 dated 20-8-1985, which was published in the Bangladesh Gazette (Extra-ordinary) on 21-8-1985. The original Sub-Rules (3) and (4) of Rule 11 of the Rules were as follows:—

"11. Suspension:— (1)

(2)   ..........

(3) Where a penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service imposed upon a Government servant is set aside or declared or rendered void in consequence of, or by a decision of, a Court of law or Administrative Tribunal and the authority, on consideration of the circumstances of the case, decides to hold a further inquiry against him on the allegation on which the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement was originally imposed the Government servant shall be deemed to have been placed under suspension by the authority from the date of original order of dismissal, removal as compulsory retirement and shall continue to remain under suspension until further orders. In such an eventuality, the limitation imposed under Rule 7(9) shall count from the date of decision to proceed against the accused following the Court decision.

(4) Further inquiry under sub-rule (3) against a Government servant shall not be held unless the decision to do so taken within thirty working days from the date of decision of the Court or Administrative Tribunal."

18. Subsequently the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 were amended and sub-Rule (2), last portion of sub-Rule (3) and sub-Rule (4) were omitted by the notification contained in SRO 304-Law/89/-EM (Rules-5) ID/88 dated 13-9-1989. After amendment of Sub-Rule 3 of Rule 11 of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1989 Rule 11 (3) stands as follows:

"11. Suspension:—

(1)  .............

(2)   ..............

(3) Where a penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement from service imposed upon a government servant is set aside or declared or rendered void in consequence of, or by a decision of, a Court of law or Administrative Tribunal and the authority, on consideration of the circumstances of the case, decided to hold a further inquiry against him on the allegation on which the penalty of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement was original .shall be deemed to have been placed under suspension by the authority from the date of original order of dismissal, removal as compulsory retirement and shall continue to remain under suspension until further orders. (4) * * * * *

19. Therefore, by making amendment to Rule 11 vide SRO 304-Law/89/EM (Rules-5) ID/88 dated 13-9-1989 the limitation clause for taking decision to hold further inquiry against any Government servant was omitted. Now, the question arises whether upon such omission the concerned authority has been legally authorized to take decision to hold such further inquiry at any time, whether they wish or event after the expiry of the statutory period 01 limitations under sub-sections (2) and (2A) of section 6 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 for preferring any appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against any order of decision of any Administrative Tribunal.

20. Under section 4(l) of the Act an Administrative Tribunal has the exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine applications made by any person in the service of the Republic or of any statutory public authority in respect of the terms and conditions of his service or in respect of any action taken against him in relation to his service.

21. Section 6(1) of the Act provides that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal shalt have jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals from any order or decision of an Administrative Tribunal.

22. But section 6(2) of the Act limits the time to three months from the date of making of the order or decision by an Administrative Tribunal for preferring appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against the order or decision.

23. Section 6(2A) of the Act provides that an appeal may be admitted after the period of three months specified in section 6(2) but not later than six months, if that appellant satisfies the Administrative Appellate Tribunal that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within three months.

24. Therefore, whatever may be the cause, no appeal can be preferred to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against any order or decision of an Administrative Tribunal after six months from the date of making of the order or decision.

25. Section 6 (3) of the Act provides that the decision of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in an appeal shall, subject to section 6A, be final.

26. Section 6A envisages that the provisions of Article 103 of the Constitution shall apply in relation of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal as they apply in relation to the High Court Division.

27. Therefore, section 6 (3) read with section 6A contemplates that the decision of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in an appeal shall be final subject to the decision of the Appellate Division on appeal, if any, against the decision of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal.

28. Thus, from successive readings of sections 4 (1), 6 (1), 6 (2), 6 (2A), 6 (3) and 6 (4) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 it appears that if no appeal is preferred to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against any order or decision of an Administrative Tribunal, on the expiry of three months or in some exceptional circumstances on the expiry of six months, as may be the case, from the date of making of the order or decision, the legal right of the person acquired through the order or decision passed by the Administrative Tribunal under section-4 (1) of the Act becomes final.

29. Rule 26 (a) of the Government Servants Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 ensures that the Rules shall not deprive any person of any right or privilege under any other law. Rule 26 runs, as follows:

"26. Rules not to deprive any per-son of any right or privilege under any other law—Nothing in these rules shall deprive any person of any right or privilege to which he is entitled—

(a) under any law; or

(b) under the terms of any contract or agreement subsisting immediately before the date of the commencement of these rules between such person and the Government."

30. Therefore, Rule 11 (3) or any other Rule of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 does not deprive any person of his legal right acquired under section 4 (1) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 once it becomes final. We have already found that the legal right acquired under section 4 (I) of the Act becomes final if no appeal is preferred to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against any order or decision of an Administrative Tribunal within three months or in some exceptional circumstances six within months, as may be the case, 'from the date of making of the order or decision.

31. Thus, upon successive readings of sections 4(1), 6(1), 6(2), 6(2A), 6(3) and 6A of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 along With Rule 26(a) and Rule 11(3) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985, we find that a decision to conduct further inquiry under Rule 11(3) may be taken in usual circumstances within three months or in exceptional circumstances within six months from the date of making of the order or decision under section 4(1) by the Administrative Tribunal if no appeal is preferred against the order or decision under section 6(1) within three months or six months as required corresponding circumstances under 6(2) or section 6(2A) of the Act. It is tool specify more clearly that in any circumstances, no decision to conduct further inquiry under Rule 11 (3) can be legally taken after six months from the date of making of the order or decision by an Administrative Tribunal under section 4(1) of the Act.

32. It is envisaged that Rule 11(3) applies only after making of a decision or an order by a 'Court of Law' or by an 'Administrative Tribunal'. But Administrative Tribunal does not include the 'Administrative Appellate Tribunal' under the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980. Similarly, in Rule 11(3) 'Court of Law' does not include any 'Appellate Court'. Therefore, in view of the discussions made before, a decision to conduct any further inquiry under Rule 11(3) after making of a decision or an order by a Court of Law, is to be taken within the time limit prescribed under that very law for preferring any appeal against the decision or order, but the respondents cannot hover on the matter for unlimited period to defeat the right of the petitioner.

<u>33. In the present case, the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal by the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 passed in. Administrative Tribunal Case No. 19 of 2002 declared the order dated 26-12-1993 dismissing the petitioner from his service and the order dated 27-2-1996 dismissing the departmental appeal of the petitioner illegal, inoperative and void with a direction on the respondents to reinstate the petitioner in his service. Therefore, by the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 the petitioner acquired a legal right under section 4(1) of the Act to be reinstated in his service subject to any appeal to the Administrative Tribunal tinder section 6(1) of the Act. But the respondents did not prefer any appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002. Therefore whatever might have been the reason for not ;preferring any appeal to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002, the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 became final at best after six months from 1-1-9-2002 i.e. on and from II-3- 2003. Thus, the petitioner's legal right acquired under section 4(1) of the Act became final from 11-3-2003. But the impugned decision under impugned Rule 11 (3) was not taken before 1I-3-2003 and it was taken only on 23-7-2006 vide impugned Memo No. Sal-At-Opinion-31 / 2006/579 dated 23-7-2006 and the same was communicated to the petitioner only vide impugned Memo No. DC: Bari/Uma- 15/93/ Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006 (Annexure-B).</u>

<u>34. Therefore, in view of the provision of Rule 26(a) read with section 4(1) and section 6(1) of the Act, the impugned Memos dated 23-7-2006 and 28-8-2006 issued in intention to conduct 're-inquiry' purportedly under impugned Rule 11 (3) in the same allegations, which gave rise to Administrative Tribunal Case No. 19 of 2002, neither did legally dislodge the finality of the judgment and order dated "11-9- 2002 nor did the same deprive the petitioner of his legal right acquired under section 4(1) of the Act and, as such, the impugned Memos are liable to be declared to have been issued with-out lawful authority and are of no legal effect.</u>

<u>35. We have already found that without preferring any appeal against the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 passed under section 4(1) of the Act and without reinstating the petitioner in his service for about four years, the respondents having resorted to impinged Rule 11(3) took decision to conduct 're-inquiry' by the impugned Memos dated 23-7-2006 and 28-8-2006. Such being the state of affairs, we find merits in the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner with reference to the case of Dr Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201 that the impugned Memos were issued main fide and out of malice both in law and fact. Therefore, the impugned Memos even on this score only are liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.</u>

36. It appears from the impugned Memo dated 23-7-2006 that thereby a 're-inquiry' was directed purportedly under the impugned Rule 11(3), but the impugned Rule 11(3) provides for 'further inquiry' and not any 're-inquiry' in the allegations and, as such, we find that the impugned Memo dated 23-7-2006 being issued directing 're-inquiry' is  further liable to be declared to have been issued violating the pro-visions of impugned Rule 11(3) itself, without lawful authority and the impugned Memo dated 28-8-2006 being issued in pursuance thereof is also liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

37. Upon thorough reading of the impugned Rule 11(3), we find merit in the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner that the impugned Rule 11 (3) does not provide for any guidelines or principles for conducting any further inquiry, which may lead to arbitrary and discriminatory exercise of the discretionary power under the impugned Rule 11(3) and accordingly, the petitioner challenged the vires of the impugned Rule 11(3). But as per the law enunciated by the Appellate Division in the case Dr Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201 and in the case of BADC vs Md Shamsul Haque Mazumder, 60 DLR (AD) 152, when a case can be disposed of without striking down the law but giving relief to the petitioner, that course is always better than striking down the law. Accordingly, we do not find any necessity for striking down the impugned Rule 11(3), but we have already found upon elaborate discussion that the impugned Memos are liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

<u>38. In view of the findings made above, we find that the order of dismissal from service of the petitioner being set aside by the Administrative Tribunal, the petitioner is entitled to be treated to have all through been in his service in the eye of law.</u>

<u>39. It appears from the discussions made before that the writ petition involves interpretations of sections 4, 6 and 6A of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 and, Rules 11 and 26 of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. Thus we further find merits in the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner on the question of maintainability of the Rule Nisi. Therefore, we hold that the Rule Nisi is maintainable.</u>

<u>40. On the findings and observations made before, we are inclined to make the Rule absolute in part. Accordingly, the impugned Memo No. Sal/AT/Opinion-31 /2006-579 dated 23-7-2006 and Memo No. DC: Bari/ Uma-115/93/- Nezarat-541 dated 28-8-2006, Annexure-B are hereby declared to have been issued without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.</u>

41. The respondents are further directed to reinstate the petitioner in his service in compliance with the judgment and order dated 11-9-2002 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Barisal in Administrative Tribunal Case No. 19 of 2002 and to pay him all arrears of his salary and allowances within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

However, there would be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: In this Rule Nisi the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the ex parte decree dated 23-9-2003 (decree signed on 30-9-2003) and the provision of section 19(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the order dated 19-6-2004 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners and proceeding of the said Artha Rin Execution No. 4 of 2003 pending in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

2. The material fact, in short, for disposal of this Rule is that the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Case No. 3 of 2002 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Jhenaidah impleading the petitioners for realisation of Taka 10,63,867. The defendants duly appeared in the suit and filed joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint.

3. Ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte by the Adalat vide judgment and decree dated 23-9-2003 (decree signed on 30-9-2003.

4. Against the said ex parte judgment and decree dated 23-9-2003 the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2003 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Jhenaidah for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 23-9-2003.

5. The learned Judge of the Adalat upon hearing the parties disallowed the said Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2003 on the ground that the petitioners did not deposit 10% of the decretal amount as per provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter called the Ain, 2003).

6. In usual course the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank, put the decree into execution by filing the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 in order to realise the decretal amount including interest by selling the petitioners' mortgaged property.

7. During pendency of the execution case the decree-holder-Bank filed an application under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter called the AM, 2003) praying for passing an order of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The Adalat, on consideration of the materials on record, issued warrant of arrest by his order dated 19-6-2004.

8. In this backdrop, the petitioners approached this Court in an application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr Abdul Jalil, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, in the course of argument after placing the writ petition along with Annexure submits that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, under misconception of law and facts, most illegally and mechanically after rejecting the application for adjournment filed by the defendant-petitioners took up the case for ex parte hearing and passed the impugned ex parte judgment and decree dated 23-9-2003 which is not tenable in law. He next submits that the provision of section 19(3) of the Ain, 2003 depositing 10% of the decretal amount while filing a petition for setting-aside ex parte decree is arbitrary and violative of the provisions of the Constitution and, as such, the same is liable to be struck down.

10. Mr Abdul Jalil further submits that the Adalat without giving any chance to enable the petitioners to make an effective representation passed the impugned order of warrant of arrest on the basis of the application under section 34 of the Ain, 2003 filed by the decree-holder bank and, as such, the impugned order of warrant of arrest dated 19-6-2004 should be declared to have been, passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

11. Lastly, Mr Abdul Jalil contends that in view of the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003, an Execution Case has to be disposed of within a period of 90 days or at least within the next sixty days but the present Execution Case has been filed on 15-12-2003 in which 90+60= 150 days has already been expired and therefore, the continuation of the proceeding of the Execution Case is clear violation of the Mandatory Provision of section 37 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and hence at any rate the impugned proceeding of the execution case is liable to be declared illegal and void.

12. On the other hand, Mrs Khursheed Jahan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank by filing affidavit-in-opposition supports the impugned judgment and decree as well as the proceeding of the Execution Case, which were, according to her, just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate in the course of argument after placing the affidavit-in-opposition, straight forward submits that the instant writ petition was filed challenging judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which is misconceived and not maintainable in law, inasmuch as by now it has been well settled that no writ petition lies against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat since there is a forum/specific provision in the Ain for seeking remedy against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Mrs Khursheed Jahan in support of her submissions relied on the cases reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD) 6 & 59 DLR (AD) 6.

13. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates for the respective parties.

14. We have perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary affidavit and other materials on record. In order to appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties from a correct angle it would be convenient for us to decide first of all as to the question of maintainability of the writ petition.

15. In the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, where it has been decided as follows:

The petitioner, without filing any appeal, filed an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, namely, Writ Petition No. 892 of 1991 which was dismissed summarily by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 30-6-91 on the ground that the petitioner has an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal The petition is dismissed."

16. In the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, where the principle has been laid down in the following terms:

"The law is now settled that since specific provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree."

17. In the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6, it has been decided:

"In view of the decisions quoted above we are led to irresistible conclusion that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant by not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain the writ petition."

18. For a reading of the above quoted uniform decisions of our Apex Court, we find a clear view of the law as it stands today that an application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not lie against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat since there being specific provision in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent Bank that the instant writ petition is misconceived and not maintainable.

19. In the case of Anisur Rahman @ KM Ziaul Haque vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 12 BLC 22, where it has been observed that the provisions of section 19 of the Ain, 2003 giving right to the borrowers to redress against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, whether ex parte or contested, it cannot be said that such defaulting borrowers have lost their fundamental right of protection of law or to be treated in accordance with law as enshrined in Article 31 of the Constitution.

20. Thereafter, we find no possible reason to differ with the above view taken by this. Accordingly, we find no reason for interference with the provision of section 19 of the Ain, 2003 in the Rule.

21. To meet the contention of Mr Abdul Jalil, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, that the continuation of the proceeding of the execution case beyond 90+60=150 days is clear violation of the mandatory provision of section 37 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, we have examined the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 as best as we could do. Section 37 of the Ain, 2003 provides a time-frame for disposal of the execution case, although the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 does not provide for the consequence if the proceeding of the execution case runs beyond 150 days.

22. Thus, it is apparent that the requirement of time-frame for disposal of an execution case as laid down in section 37 of the Ain, 2003, is merely directory and not mandatory. So, it cannot be said that if the execution case is not disposed of within 90+60=150 days it will be automatically stopped or dismissed. This view of ours finds support in the case of Khurshed Alam (Md) vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat-1 reported in 12 BLC 592.

23. In that view of the matter, we find no merit in the submissions of Mr Abdul Jalil.

24. Now, the question that calls for consideration, whether the order of warrant of arrest passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin Execution No. 4 of 2003 suffers from any legal infirmity or not.

25. In deciding this question, we feel it necessary to examine the provision of section 34 of the Ain, 2003 which deals with the power of the Adalat to pass an order of civil jail/ warrant of arrest.

26. Section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is reproduced below:

৩৪। দেওয়ানী আটকাদেশঃ(১) উপ ধারা (১২) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, অর্থ ঋণ আদালত, ডিক্রীদার কর্তৃক দাখিলকৃত দরণাস্তের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে, ডিক্রীর টাকা পরিশোধে বাধ্য করিবার প্রয়াস হিসাবে, দায়িককে ৬(ছয়) মাস পর্যন্ত দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখিতে পারিবে ৷

২) উপধারা (১) এর উল্লিখিত বিধান, মূল ঋণ গ্রহীতার মৃত্যুর কারণে পারিবারিক উত্তরাধিকার আইন অনুযায়ী স্থলাভিষিক দায়িক ওয়ারিশদের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হইবে না ৷

৩) জারী মামলা কোন কোম্পানী (Company), যৌথ কারবারী প্রতিষ্ঠান (Firm) অথবা অন্য কোন নিয়মবদ্ধ সংস্থা (Corporate body) এর বিরুদ্ধে কার্যকর করিতে বিবাদী দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা আবশ্যক হইলে, উল্লিখিত কোম্পানী, যৌথ কারবারী প্রতিষ্ঠান বা নিয়মবদ্ধ সংস্থা আইন বা বিধি মোতাবেক যে সকল স্বাভাবিক ব্যক্তির (natural person) সমন্বয়ে গঠিত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে, সেই সকল ব্যক্তি এককভাবে ও যৌথভাবে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটকের জন্য দায়ী হইবেন ৷

৪) উপ ধারা (৩) এর বিধান এইরুপ কোন ব্যক্তির বিরুদ্ধে কার্যকর হইবে না যিনি ডিক্রীর সংশিষ্ঠ ঋণ গ্রহন্যের পরবর্তীতে উত্তরাধিকার সূত্রে উপরিউলিখিত কোন ব্যক্তি বা ব্যক্তিবর্গের স্থলাভিষিক্ত হইয়াহেন।

৫।উপ ধারা ৯১) বা (৩) এর অধীনে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক কোন ব্যক্তি, ডিক্রীর দাবী সম্পূর্ণরুপে পরিশোধ না করা পর্যন্ত, অথবা ৬(ছয়) মাসের সময়সীমা অতিক্রম না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, যাহা পূর্বে হয়, দেওয়ানী কারাগার হইতে মুক্তি লাভ করিবে না, এবং ডিক্রীর সম্পূর্ণ টাকা পরিশোধ করার সংগে সংগে আদালত তাহাকে দেওয়ানী কারাগার হইতে মুক্তির নির্দেশ প্রদান করিবে।

৬) উপ ধারা (৫) এর বিধান সত্বেও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক দায়িক যদি ডিক্রীদারের অপরিশোধিত পাওনার ২৫% এর সমপরিমান অর্থ নগদ পরিশোদ করিয়া এই মর্মে বন্ড প্রদান করেন যে, তিনি পরবর্তী ৯০(নব্বই)দিনের মধ্যে অবশিষ্ট পাওনা পরিশোধ করিবেন, তবে সেক্ষেত্রে আদালত দায়িককে মুক্তি প্রদান করিবে ৷

৭) উপ-ধারা(৬)এ উল্লিখিত বন্ডের শর্ত মোতাবেক যদি দায়িক অবশিষ্ট পাওনা পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হন, তবে তিনি পুনরায় গ্রেফতার ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে পুনরায় আটকাদেশ হইলে, উহা ছয় মাস পর্যন্ত বহালযোগ্য নতুন আটকাদেশ হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে।

৮) এই আইনের অধীনে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটককৃত ব্যক্তির ভরন পোষণ খরচ সরকার কর্তৃক বিচারাদী আসামীর অনুরুপ খরচের ন্যায় বহন করা হইবে, এবং পরবর্তীকালে সরকার ডিক্রীদারের নিকট হইতে সরকারী পাওনা হিসাবে উক্ত খরচের অর্থ আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার দায়িকের নিকট হইতে মামলার খরচ বাবদ উক্ত অর্থ আদায় করিতে পাবিবে ৷

৯ ৷ এই ধারার অধীনে আদালত কোন দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করার আদেশ প্রদান করিবে না, যদি না তৎপূর্বে অন্ততঃ একটি নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠিত হইয়া থাকে এবং উহার দ্বারা ডিক্রীদারের প্রাপ্য পরিপূর্ণভাবে আদায় হইয়া থাকে ৷

১০) যদি কোন কারনে উপ ধারা (৯) এর অধীন একটিও নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠান করা সম্ভব না হয় তবে সেই ক্ষেত্রে দায়িককে সরাসরি গ্রেফতার ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা যাইবে ৷

১১) ১৮ (আঠার) বৎসরের কম বয়স্ক কোন ব্যক্তিকে এই ধারার অধীনে ডিক্রী কার্যকর করার নিমিত্ত গ্রেফতার এবং দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা বা রাখা যাইবে না৷

১২) এই আইনের অধীনে কোন ডিক্রী বা আদেশ বাস্তবায়নের উদ্দেশ্যে পরিচালিত জারী মামলায়, জারী মামলায় সংখ্যা একাধিক হইলেও কোন একজন দায়িককে গ্রেফতার করিয়া পরিপূর্ণ মেয়াদের জন্য একবার দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখা হইলে, তাহাকে পুনরায় গ্রেফতার করা ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা যাইবে না।

১৩) এই ধারার অধীনে কোন দায়িককে আংশিক বা পূর্ণ মেয়াদের জন্য দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখার কারণে তিনি দেনার দায় হইতে মূক্ত গণ্য হইবেন না, এবং এই আইনের অধীন নির্ধারিত তামাদি দ্বারা বারিত না হইলে, তাহার বিরুদ্ধে নতুন করিয়া জারী মামলা দায়ের করা যাইবে৷

<u>27. From a combined reading of those sub-sections of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it manifests that the Adalat is empowered to pass an order of Warrant of Arrest/ Civil Imprisonment directly on the basis of an application filed by the decree-holder bank when no auction sale is possible to be held for any reason.</u>

<u>28. We have examined the application filed by the decree-holder-Bank under section 34 of the Ain, 2003 for passing an order of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors and the impugned order of warrant of arrest. It appears that on two occasions the Adalat after due compliance of law took attempt to sell the mortgaged property by auction but the property was not sold due to non-availability of the purchaser. So, in any view of the matter, the learned Judge of the Adalat committed no illegality in passing the impugned order of warrant of arrest. The learned Judge of the Adalat appears to have considered all the legal aspects. We therefore, do not find any merit in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners.</u>

29. By now we have covered the points raised by the learned Advocates for the respective parties.

30. In view of our discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs and the uniform decisions of the highest Court vis-a-vis the law by now it is clear that the instant Rule must fail.

31. In the result, the Rule is discharged with a cost of Taka 5,000 (five thousand). The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

32. The Artha Rin Adalat, Jhenaidah is directed to proceed with the Execution Case No. 4 of 2003 expeditiously.

Communicate the order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali J : All these Writ Petitions arise out of the property of the Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia Waqf Estate. As common question of facts and law are involved in these writ petitions they were heard together and are being disposed of by this common Judgment which will govern all the writ petitions.

2. In writ petition No. 9256 of 2005 Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to take necessary steps to take over possession of the said Kazir Bazar Hat situated within the Sylhet City Corporation (More fully described in Paragraph 3B of the petition) and to lease it out in public auction as per the guide-line of Hat/Bazar set out by the respondent No.1.

3. The petitioner filed instant writ petition for public interest against inaction of the respondent No.1, 2, 4 and 5 to take necessary steps to take over possession of the Kazir Bazar Hat and Bazar (a cattle market) situated within the Jurisdiction of Sylhet City Corporation and lease out the same in public auction as per the guide line of Hat and Bazar set out by respondent No.1 according to section 20 sub section 2(a) and sub-section 5(1) (c) and sub section 6 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and that the respondent No.6 is not the proper authority to lease out any Hat and Bazar as the property vested in the Government automatically by operation of law and the respondent No.5 is the proper authority to lease out the Hat and Bazar in public auction as per guide line of Hat and Bazar.

4. Further case of the petitioner is that Kazir Bazar Hat and Bazar is a cattle market situated in the middle of Sylhet City Corporation and the cattle market in the whole Sylhet City.

5. In the year 1922 with the approval of the Assam Government KB Ahia Waqf Estate was established empowering the Government as trustee, As per terms and condition of Waqf deed the present Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet is the ex-officio Mutawalli. The said Waqf Estate is a Waqf-ul-Lillah. The said Kazir Bazar Hat was established in the year 1952 within the khas land of the said Waqf Estate and the Hat and Bazar take place in every Friday and Monday of the week.

6. The said Kazir Bazar Hat measuring an area of 1.3555 acre situated at Dag No. 1354, Khatian No. 1 Serial No. 2239 under Sylhet Municipal Area. In the year 1354 BS, the said Kazir Bazar Hat was leased out to one Mokon Miah for a period of 6(six) years. However it was continued till 1373 BS.

7. Before expiry of said lease period, Mr Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1970 for declaration of his statutory occupancy right and right of successive renewals of lease. The said suit was disposed of vide order dated 18-3-1974 on the terms of compromise and agreed upon that the lease period will continue. But the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept rent from the said Mokon Miah. Consequently, the said Mokon Miah filed another Title Suit being Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 against the said KB Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent occupancy right of the said Hat and for permanent injunction restraining the KB Ahia Waqf Estate not to disturb the possession of the said Mokon Miah or evicting him from the said land (Hat) by force and also obtained an order of temporary injunction to that effect. The said order was upheld by the High Court Division as well as up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

8. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices for obtaining temporary injunction by filing suit and managed to keep the possession of the said Hat against the interest of the Waqf Estate. In this situation, the respondent No.3, Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 issued letter to the respondent No.6, the Divisional Commissioner stating that the KB Ahia Waqf Estate has been suffering from huge financial loss due to long pendency of Civil suits. Subsequently, on an application of the respondent No. 7, the said Kazir Bazar Hat was leased out in her favour in that view of the matter respondent No. 3 wrote a letter requesting the respondent No.6 to take necessary steps to execute a fresh lease deed in favour of respondent No.7 on the terms and conditions of the letter. As per the said letter of the respondent No. 3 a lease deed was prepared and vide Memo No. O:Pro:/Sylhet/ 823 dated 23-11-1997 the lease deed was approved. Accordingly the lease deed was executed in favour of respondent No. 7. It was stipulated in the said lease deed that the respondent No.7 would pay an amount of Taka 1,30,677.35 as premium for the lease period from 1977 to 1995 while she was in possession of the Kazir Bazar Hat. The lease was valued only Taka 9,500/- for the year 1997 by the respondent No. 6. The respondent No. 7 had given an undertaking to pay lease money since 1977 as per lease deed. Subsequently the lease of the said Kazir Bazar Hat was renewed in favour of the respondent No. 7 on 22 November, 2004 with an amount of Taka 1,000 for the year 2004-2005.

9. Further case of the petitioner is that the said Hat was illegally leased out to the respondent No. 7 with a nominal value and the respondent No. 7 in collaboration of the respondent No.6 has been enjoying the possession of the said Hat illegally. The further case of the petitioner is that the Hat and Bazar automatically vested in the Government by operation of law. The petitioner on 10-4-2005 applied to the respondent No. 2 with a request to take over possession and lease out the said Hat as per guide line of Hat/Bazar under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

10. In response to the said intimation and initiation of the petitioner, the respondent No. 5 submitted a report vide Memo No. 101 dated 7-6-2005 to the respondent No.1 But no action was taken by the respondent No. 1 to take over possession of the said Hat. The further case of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 6 has/had no authority to lease out Hat and Bazar to any person for which the Government is being deprived of its revenue.

11. The further case of the petitioner is that Hat/Bazar situated within Sylhet City Corporation could not be legally owned and possessed by the respondent No. 6 due to whole sale acquisition of Khas land by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Management) Ordinance, 1959. The further case of the petitioner is that under section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the cattle market is a "Hat" according to the definition of section 20(2a) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The land or structure therein of a Hat or Bazar has been excluded from retainable land and acquirable by the Government. sub-section 2(a) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have retrospective effect of excluding Hat and Bazar from the category of retainable land and Hat and Bazar vested in the Government from the notification under section 3(2) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956 and as such no fresh notification is required for inclusion of a Hat and Bazar. The further case of the petitioner is that section 20(5)(i)(c) excludes Waqf land from operation of sub-section (1), (2) and (3) of section 20, those subsections deal with retainable land. The provision of sub-section 6 of section 20 again excludes Hat or Bazar from the operation of sub section (c) of clause (i) of subsection (5) and Clause (ii) of that subsection i.e. Hat/Bazar are not retainable on the ground that those Hat and Bazar are Waqf Estate.

12. Further case of the petitioner is that Waqf Estate is not entitled to retain Hat /Bazar. Hat and Bazar land stands acquired on the date of notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In the meantime, the Government has not taken over possession of the land of Waqf Estate having Hat and Bazar, the Mutawalli holding right title or any interest in the land having Hat/Bazar continued to manage as the agent of the Government till taking over possession. As per provision of the proviso (i) to section 10(a)(3)(b) no Mutawalli is competent to transfer or create any encumbrance or charge on any such interest over the said khas land in any manner except by a temporary lease not exceeding 1 year. Any transfer or any encumbrances or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision is null and void. The provision of section 39(1)(a) is clear with non-obstinate clause that land of Hat and Bazar under Waqf Estate is subject to acquisition and are entitled to compensation. The provision of section 2 of Hat and Bazar (State Acquisition) Ordinance 1959 provides establishment of any Hat and Bazar by any person other than the Government. The Local Administration may establish Hat and Bazar with the prior approval of the Government. Since notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has already been made. No fresh notification for Acquisition of Hat and Bazar of the Waqf Estate is necessary. Since there is no encumbrance in any manner in the Waqf Estate, even if there is any encumbrance in the property shall be null and void. The nullity of such encumbrance takes effect from the inception that means the encumbrance is void and ab initio.

13. Further case of the petitioner is that Kazir Bazar Hat managed by the Waqf Estate is situated within the Sylhet City Corporation is not retainable properly by the Waqf Estate. In view of clear provision of law, the Hat and Bazar is still retained by the Waqf Estate as their private property is wholly illegal and is being held in total violation of Provisions of law. The purported lease granted by the Waqf Authority as Waqf Estate from 1947 onward without any auction is in total violation of the provision of section 10(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. According to the provision of the said Act such continuance of lease without any auction is a nullity.

14. Further case of the petitioner is that inaction of the respondent No. 1-5 in not taking over the possession and giving public auction of the said Hat as per guide line for the management of Hat and Bazar is being contrary to the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Such inaction is subject to rectification and remedy lies under the direction to hold the public auction of the said Kazir Bazar Hat. Consequently, the petitioner filed instant writ petition and obtained Rule.

15. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Dr AKM Ali with Mr Md Anowarul Islam for the petitioner submits that Kazir Bazar Hat is situated in the City of Sylhet. One KB Anis established a Waqf Estate in the year 1922 and Kazir Bazar Hat was established in 1952 one of the property of Waqf Estate. He further submitted that according to State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the Government acquired land and building of a Hat and Bazar including other thing under section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Management Ordinance 1951) and, as such, the Kazir Bazar Hat is a Acquired property of the Government and that the said Hat should be leased out according to the guide line of Hat and Bazar vide Memo No. Proje e-/Ha-5/2000/408(5272) dated 20-7-2002 issued by the respondent No. 1 under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. But without complying the aforementioned guide line the said Hat and Bazar leased out by the respondent No. 6 in collaboration with respondent No. 7 with a nominal value. He further submitted that Hat and Bazar automatically vested to the Government by operation of law. He further submitted that the said Kazir Bazar Hat was established in the year 1952 within the land of the Waqf Estate which was given lease of the said Hat and Bazar by the Waqf Estate in the year 1354 BS to one Mokon Mia for a period of (six) years, which was continued until 1373 BS During the continuance of the said lease Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1970 for declaration of his statutory occupancy right and right of successive renewals of the lease. The said suit was disposed of by an order dated 18-3-1974 on the terms of compromise, it was asserted that the lease will be continued. But subsequently the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept rent from the said Mokon Miah. Consequently the said Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 against the said Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent heritable lease and for permanent injunction restraining the authority from disturbing the possession of the said Mokon Miah or evicting him from the said premises. The said Mokon Miah obtained the order of temporary injunction against the eviction. The said order was also confirmed by the High Court Division as well as by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

16. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices for obtaining temporary injunction, managed to keep the possession of the said Hat and Bazar as against the interest of the Waqf Estate. Consequently, the respondent No. 3, Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 informed to the respondent No. 6 ex-officio Mutawalli that the suits are pending for a long period and the KB Ahia Waqf Estate has been suffering from financial loss. Subsequently the Waqf Authority without any public auction leased out the said Kazir Bazar Hat to Mrs Hamida Khatun daughter of Mokon Miah previous leasee. In that view of matter respondent No. 3 requested the respondent No. 6 to take necessary steps to execute a fresh lease deed in favour of respondent No. 7 on the terms and conditions as mentioned the said letter.

17. As per said letter of the respondent No. 3 a lease deed was prepared and it was approved. Accordingly the lease deed was executed in favour of respondent No. 7 which shows that the lease deed was a renewal of previous lease executed with the said Mokon Miah. According to the said lease deed the respondent No. 7 has to pay an amount of Tk 1,30,677.35 as premium for the lease period from 1977 to 1995 the period on which the suits were pending for which no amount was collected. She has been enjoying the possession of the Hat. The lease period yearly valued only TK 9,500/ for the year 1997 though the respondent No. 7 gave an undertaking to the collector that she will pay all the dues during the period of litigation. Since 1977 the lease of the said Kazir Bazar Hat was renewed annually in favour of the respondent No.7 and only on 22nd November, 2004 lease was granted for the period 2004-2005 with an amount of TK 1,00,000/ only.

18. The petitioner having concerned for the protection of public property as well as for the public interest of the country filed instant writ petition to protect and preserve the public property under Article 21 of the Constitution and filed various application to the authority concerned requesting them to take possession of the Hat and Bazar and also requested to lease out the Hat and Bazar as per guide line of Hat and Bazar under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

19. In response to the said application of the petitioner, the respondent No. 5 submitted a report on 7-6-2005 but no steps was taken nor the property was taken over by the authority, though the Government is being deprived of its revenue. Finding no other alternative, the petitioner filed instant writ petition.

20. Mr TH Khan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing with Mr JN Deb and Mr Helaluddin Mollah and Mr AKM Shamsul Huq by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit in opposition for the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 submitted that the property originally belonged to Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia who subsequently in the year 1922 established Waqf Estate as Waqf-ul-Lillah known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate under the approval of the then Government of Asham. Since then the case property along with other properties have been possessing and enjoying by the Waqf Estate. The Secretary, Ministry of Land, Respondent No. 2 also directed to the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet, Maulvi Bazar, Sunamganj not to disturb the peaceful possession of the Waqf Estate and according to the said direction, the respondent No. 6 Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 for correction of record which is still pending for determination and another Title Suit No.72 of 1999 in respect of permanent injunction was decreed in favour of the Waqf Estate against which no appeal was preferred. The petitioner has no locus standi to file instant writ petition. He further submitted that the property in question is Waqf ul Lillah and the income of the said Waqf-ul-Lillah being used for the benefit of charitable purpose. He further submitted that the whole sale acquisition under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not applicable in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate. Moreover, the Government did not acquired the property of the Waqf Estate till today nor the Government paid any compensation or award in favour of the Waqf authority till today nor there was any direction to handover possession of the Waqf Properties. He further submitted that the said Waqf Estate enrolled under Provisional Government of Asam which was subsequently, enrolled after partition of Bengal to the Waqf Administrator of East Pakistan under EC No. 13071 and before declaration of Sylhet Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the Mutawalli and after declaration of Division the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate thus Managing the same, at the same time the Divisional Commissioner became the representative of the Government. Since at the time of SA operation some of the properties of the Waqf Estate was wrongly record in the name of Government as khas Land of the Government, Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet wrote a letter to the Secretary Ministry of Land, the Secretary, Ministry of Religious and the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet to hold an enquiry and lastly the Divisional commissioner on 8-10-1987 issued a letter under Memo No. Vum-71/87/684 / (1) 4 stating that “এস্টেটের যে সকল সম্পত্তি ভুল ক্রমে সরকারী খাস খতিয়ান রেকর্ড করা হইয়াছে সেগুলি সংশোধনের ব্যবস্থা নিতে অনুরোধ জানাচ্ছে।”

21. Thereafter the Ministry of Land, respondent No. 2 vide Memo No. Vu:Ma: Sha/5/ Waqf/Sylhet/ 177/91(3) dated 5-8-1991 directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj, Habigonj, Moulvibazar not to interfere in the function of the Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Waqf Estate in any manner and also to take proper steps for correction of wrong record. But inspite of the said memo, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar trying to disturb the possession of the Waqf Estate. In such situation, one Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Sylhet praying for permanent injunction against the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar. After hearing of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit against which no appeal has been preferred thus the said decree of permanent injunction is still in force. Another suit being Title Suit No. 07 of 2002 in respect of correction of wrong record is still pending before the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj.

22. The Government revenue head of Sylhet i.e. Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and after declaration of Sylhet Division the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became Revenue head and Mutawalli and he has been managing and controlling and possessing all the Waqf Estate. He further submitted that from 1922 as per terms of registered Waqf Deed and as per approval of the then Asham provisional Government. By giving lease of the Waqf properties in favour of different persons including the present Kazir Bazar Hat and Bazar earning the money 100% of which is expending for the purpose of public interest and for the interest of other religious and charitable establishment. Since the property is the Waqf property, the Government has no jurisdiction to acquire the property of the Waqf Estate and that since the property is Waqf-ul-Lillah and as per section 20(5)(1(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the Kazir Bazar Hat was leased out on 15-12-2005 in favour of one Ms Hamida Khatun for the year 2006 only and the said leasee is in possession of the lease property.

23. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 before the Joint District Judge, Habigonj against the Government and others praying for declaration of Title in respect of the suit property including the land in question. The said Title Suit is still pending for final hearing. He further submitted that one of the leasee of the Government i.e. Md Shamsul Alam has filed writ petition No. 5164 of 2003 claiming some land of the Waqf Estate as the leasee of the Government. But the Rule was discharged with cost by the judgment and order dated 29-3-2005. Ministry of Land respondent No. 2 on 3-5-2006 wrote a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet by canceling their previous letter dated 1-1-2006 in respect of taking over possession of the case properties; which indicates that the property in question is a Waqf Property not Khas land of the Government. He further submitted that the property in question is the property of KB. Ahia Waqf Estate is 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah under section 20(5)(i)(c) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah property cannot be taken over by the Government. He further submitted that since there is a judgment and decree of permanent injunction against the Government in Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate, against which no appeal has been filed and as such the judgment and decree of the Title Suit No.72 of 1999 is binding upon the Government. Another Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 is still pending before the Second Court, Habigonj against the Government of Bangladesh in respect of the Waqf property prying for declaration of title and a such the instant writ petition is not maintainable. He further submitted that the property of the Waqf Estate is not normal. Hat and Bazar, it is the absolute property of the Waqf Estate and has been using for special purpose for cattle market for the people of the locality. Whether the property is normal Hat and Bazar under the definition of Hat, Bazar or not is a question of fact which can be decided in the civil Court not before this writ jurisdiction.

24. He further submitted that decree for permanent injunction has been granted against the Government in Title Suit No. 77 of 1999 which is binding upon the Government. The petitioner in the name of Public interest cannot unsettle the said judgment and decree of the civil Court.

25. He further submitted that another Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 is still pending before the Court of Joint District Judge, Habigonj by Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia Waqf Estate represented by Ex-officio Mutawalli, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet Division and the schedule of present writ petition is also subject-matter of the schedule of the said Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 and that the Title Suit is earlier then the instant writ petition, hence the judgment and decree has been passed in Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 and since no appeal has been preferred against said judgment and decree of the permanent injunction and if the civil Court pass a judgment and decree in that case on the same subject matter the result of the Rule of this writ petition may bring multiplicity of proceeding.

26. He further submitted that regarding the self same subject-matter of the writ petition, the predecessor of the respondent No. 7 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 363 of 1977 before the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and vide order dated 8-11-1977 the said Court directed all the parties to maintain status quo. During the pendency of the said suit one Sirajul Islam filed an application for addition of party as co-plaintiff. Being unsuccessful, he filed civil revision No. 3789 of 1997 before the High Court and obtained an order of stay and also stay all further proceeding of the suit and the said civil revision is still pending and that the representative of KB Ahia Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 104 of 1997 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 against the Government of Bangladesh, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and others and the said suit was decreed vide Judgment and decree dated 30-8-2001 by declaring that Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is entitled to hold and possess the land of the Waqf Estate and also granted permanent injunction against the defendants restraining them from disturbing possession and management till preparation of the annuity and compensation assessment Role. Against the said judgment and decree none preferred any appeal and, as such, the said judgment and decree is still in force and binding upon the defendants. The Respondent No.6 also filed Title. Suit No. 7 of 2002 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court. Habigonj against the Government and others for declaration and for correction of record of right in respect of the subject-matter of this writ petition. The said Title Suit is still pending before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj.

27. Md Mokon Miah the predecessor of the respondent No. 7 had filed Title Suit. No. 306 of 1979 before the Court of learned Munsif, Sadar, 1st Court, Sylhet which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Biswanath, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 82 of 1985 against the Waqf Estate and others for declaration of permanent heritable right of occupancy and in the alternation holding over tenancy right of the plaintiff and for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in regard to the suit land or evicting him from the suit land by force except in due process of law. In the said suit, the Government official filed written statement stating cattle market is not retainable land. The prayer for temporary injunction was allowed by trial Court which was affirmed up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 366 of 1981 and the original suit is still pending before the trial Court for disposal. In the said suit one Sirajul Islam filed an application for adding as Co-plaintiff, which was rejected against which Sirajul Islam filed Civil Revision before this Court and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 4170 of 1996 which is still pending for disposal.

28. Mr MA Mannan the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 5 Sylhet City Corporation by submitting affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the City Corporation stated that lease of cattle market in favour of Mokon Miah was granted by the Waqf Estate for 6(six) years and within his lease term he filed a suit for declaration of his occupancy right with a right of inheritance and for temporary injunction against the KB. Ahia Waqf Estate and being unsuccessful he fought up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. Further stated that suit was ultimately compromised by the daughter of Mokon Miah Ms Hamida Khatun who filed case after case to keep the possession of the cattle market on frivolous and fraudulent steps.

29. Further stated that Mokon Miah adopted various tactics by filing suits for obtaining temporary injunction and to maintain possession of the cattle market against the interest of Waqf estate for which Waqf estate is suffering from financial loss. Further stated that deponent was not awarded any power according to letter of respondent No. 3 Further stated that the said Hat was illegally leased out to the respondent No. 7 and that Hat and Bazar automatically vested in the Government by operation of law. This deponent has no knowledge if the petitioner applied to the respondent No. 2 to take over possession of the Hat in question and to lease out the same as per guide line of the Hat and Bazar under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the respondent No. 6 illegally leased out the Hat in question and caused loss to the Government.

30. Mr Karuna Moy Chakma, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing with Enus Ali, the learned Assistant Attorney General by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of respondent No. 1 and 2 submitted that the Kazir Bazar cattle market is situated at the Northern side of East Kazir Bazar of Sylhet Town and it is the only cattle market in the Sylhet town. In the year 1922 with the approval of the Asham Government, Khan Bahadur Ahia established a Waqf Estate empowering the Government as trustee. As per term and condition of the Waqf deed the present Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became ex-officio Mutawalli. The said Waqf Estate is called KB Ahia Waqfs estate. The Kazir Bazar Cattle market was established in the year 1952 in the land of the said Waqf Estate. Usually the said Hat sits on Monday and Friday of all the weeks and the said Kazir Bazar Hat was given lease to one Mokon Miah by the authority of the Waqf Estate in the year 1354 BS and at that time when the lease period has been expired the said Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1977 for declaration of occupancy right successive renewal of lease. The said suit was disposed of on 18-34974. On the terms of compromise and it was stipulated in compromise that the lease would continue. But subsequently, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept the said Mokon Miah as leasee. The said Mokon Miah then filed another suit being Title suit No. 145 of 1976 for specific performance of contract. Another suit being Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 was filed against KB Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent heritable or transferable right of occupancy of the said hat and obtained an ad-interim order of injunction against the Waqf Estate from evicting the plaintiff petitioner. The said ad-interim order of injunction was affirmed by the High Court Division as well by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices by filing Title suit and obtained temporary injunction thus managed to keep the possession of the Hat against the interest of the Waqf Estate. Thereafter the Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 wrote a letter to the Divisional Commissioner and ex-officio Mutawalli stating that the Waqf Estate has been suffering from financial loss due to the long pendency of civil suits and these civil suits may take long time for final disposal. Subsequently due to the above reasoning the Waqf estate was leased out on the application of the respondent No. 7 Ms Hamida Khatun, the daughter of said Mokon Miah. Respondent No.3 requested the respondent No. 6 to take necessary steps to execute a lease deed in favour of respondent No. 7. The respondent No. 3 approved the deed of lease in favour of respondent No. 7 for the period of 1977 to 1995. Subsequently, the lease was granted for the year 2004-2005 fixing a lease amount of Tk. 1,00,000 The lease of the said Hat was granted by the Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Waqf Estate but not according to the guide line of Hat and Bazar.

31. He further submitted that according to the decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court reported in 28 DLR (AD) 195, property under Waqf-ul-Lillah cannot be acquired under section 20(5)(i)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, there is no question of taking over possession of the Waqf Estate by the respondents and that Kazir Bazar cattle market was established in 1952 and lease was granted on yearly basis according to the direction of the Waqf Administration and there is no order to hand over possession to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet or Sylhet City Corporation and that the Ministry of Land directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to correct the wrong recording of the Waqf Property vide Annexure-1 (A) which runs thus:
