62. First question is that as to whether the petitioner had any locus standi to file the present writ petition, in the case of Kazi Molchlesur Rahman vs Bangladesh and another reported in 26 DLR (AD) 44, (Popularly known as "Beru Bari Case) the seven general principles has been laid down that:

(1) The High Court Division does not suffer from any lack of jurisdiction under Article 102 to hear a person.

(2) The High Court Division will grant locus standi to a person who agitates a question affecting a ,constitutional issue of grave importance, posing a threat to his fundamental rights which pervade and extend to the entire territory of Bangladesh.

(3) If a fundamental right is involved, the impugned matter need not affect a purely personal right of the applicant touching him alone. It is enough if he 'shares that right in common with others.

(4) In interpreting the words "any person aggrieved", consideration of "Fundamental Rights" in part III of the Constitution is a relevant one.

(5) It is the competency of the person the claim a hearing which is at the heart of the interpretation of the words "any person aggrieved".

(6) It is a question of exercise of discretion by the High Court Division as to whether it will treat that person aggrieved or not,

(7). The High Court Division will exercise that jurisdiction upon due consideration of the facts and circumstances of each case."

63. In the instant case, the petitioner claims to have been aggrieved by the lease of Kazir Bazar Cattle Market by the Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate, which appears to us that the petitioner personally aggrieved not for the common purpose of the country as a whole.

64. Next question is that, whether Kazir Bazar Cattle Market is a property under the KB Ahia Waqf Estate or acquired under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

65. It appears that one Khan Bahadur Ahia executed a Waqf deed in the year 1922 with the approval of Asham Government measuring an area of 24,000 acres of land including the land situated in Kazir Bazar. Kazir Bazar Cattle Market has been established in the land of KB Ahia Waqf Estate and that Kazir. Bazar Cattle Market takes place every Friday and Monday of each week. The petitioner himself also admitted that Kazir Bazar Cattle Market situated in Plot No. 1354 measuring an area of 1.555 acres under Sylhet - Municipality a property of KB Ahia Waqf estate. The said Cattle Market was given lease to one Mokon Miah by the Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate in the years 1354 BS for a period of 6 (six) years which continued till 1373 BS.

66. It further appears that the Mutawalli of KB Ehia Waqf Estate, Divisional Commissioner leased out the said Cattle Market in the year 2006, it was leased out to one Ms Hamida Khatun daughter of Late Mokon Miah. Though there are suits between the parties, which are not relevant and not necessary to discuss in the instant writ petition.

67. Let us see, as to whether the said Kazir Bazar Cattle Market is retainable under the law. Though Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 filed by one of the beneficiary (Shahid Mubarak) of KB Ehia Waqf Estate who obtained a decree of permanent injunction from the civil Court in respect of schedule property of the suit, against which no appeal has been preferred by any quarter. As per section 20 (5) (i) (c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the 100%. Waqf-a-Lillah property cannot be taken over by the Government. Those properties cannot be dealt with under section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

68. Relevant portion section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, reads as follows:—

"10A Special Provisions Regarding Certain rent Receiving Interests. Held Under Waqf , Waqf-al-al Aulad, debutter or other Religious Trust-

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in clauses (e) and (ff) of sub-section (4) of section 3 or in section 6A, the provisions of this section shall apply to the cases where the [interest of a rent-receiver] held under any Waqf, Waqf-al-Aulad, debutter or other religious trust have been acquired under sub-section (1) [or sub-section (2)] of section 3, but the Government have not exercised the right to possession over such interest till the date of commencement of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (amendment) Ordinance, 1960, by starting collection of rent and cesses from the tenants holding lands immediately under such interests, or by any other means.

(2) On and from the date of acquisition of such Interests, the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, as the case may be holding such interest immediately before such date shall continue, and be deemed to have continued to manage such interests as the agent of the Government till the last day of the agricultural year [in which the] publication of the notification under subsection (2) of section 43 declaring that a Compensation Assessment-roll in respect of such interests has been finally published [is made] [ or till the time the Government exercise the right of possession over such interests, whichever is later.]

(3) Such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall, as the agent of the Government, be entitled to collect, at the rates provided in. and subject to the provisions of, sub section (4), all rents and cesses payable by the tenants to the Government in respect of such interests, and to collect the usufruct of such interest in Khas land for the period from the date of acquisition of such interests till the last day of the agricultural year [or till the exercise of the right of possession, as referred to in sub-section (2) whichever is later] and to retain the proceeds of such collection [or other income] in lieu of ad interim payments under section 6A in respect of such interests and his remuneration, subject to payment to the Government annually, in the prescribed manner, of a sum equivalent to the total of the following amounts, namely—

(a) The amounts which were, or are determined by the Collector to have (3) been, payable annually for such interests immediately before acquisition on account of revenue or rent and cesses to the Government or to the immediate superior landlord, as the case may be, and

(b) The amount that would have been assessable as tax under the Bengal Agricultural Income-Tax Act, 1944, (Bengal Act IV of 1944) in respect of the income from such interests had not the interests been acquired.

Provided that—

(i) No such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to transfer, or to create any encumbrance or charge on, any such interest in any khas land in any manner otherwise than by a temporary lease but no such temporary lease shall be given for a period exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the agricultural year in which it is 'created, nor shall any tree be cut down or building demolished, except with the previous permission of the Collector and on such terms as the Collector may prescribe in that behalf; and any transfer or any encumbrance or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision thereof  shall be null and void and the full value of any tree cut down or building demolished in such contravention shall be recoverable from the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee as an arrear of rent or land revenue;

(ii) With effect from the 1st Baisakh, 1367 BS, the amount payable under clause (a) shall be reduced by an amount equivalent to the amount which was, or is  determined by the Collector to have been, payable annually by the tenants

69. In view of the provision Of Section 10A the Government cannot take over possession of the property-of the Waqf-Estate from which income  is being used for the purpose of charitable organization.

<u>70. In the instant case, Chief Revenue Officer of the Division is the Mutawalli of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate and admittedly the Mutawalli is in possession through lease and has been  treating as an agent of the Government as contemplated under section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Which has been settled in the case of Bangladesh vs Dewan Anwar Raja Chowdluiry, being dead his heirs; Dewan Shamsul Abedin reported  in BCR 1984 (AD) 231.</u>

71. In the said case there is no discussion   of the  case of Chowdhury Tanbir Ahmad Siddiky and others vs. Province of East Pakistan and others reported in 20 DLR (SC) 144 as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

72. In that case also it was held that acquisition of the interest of Mutawalli and Sheba as rent receiver have vested with the Government with effect from date of notification issued' under section 43(2) of Chapter 5 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

73. In the instant case, there is no publication of compensation assessment roll under section 43 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act The, respondent No. 1 and 2 in their affidavit in opposition as well as supplementary affidavit in opposition has categorically admitted that no compensation assessment role has been prepared and published according to the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Rules there under and as such we find that the property in question is still the property of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate and it will remains so until the Government takes steps in accordance with law.

74. Let us see whether the petitioner can agitate the matter regarding the property of the Waqf Estates, let us see Article 102 of our Constitution, the relevant portion of which reads as follows :

"102. (1) The High Court Division on the application of any person aggrieved, may give such directions or orders to any person or authority, including any person performing any function in connection with the affairs Of the Republic, as may be appropriate for the enforcement of any of the fundamental rights Conferred by part III of this Constitution.

(2) The High Court Division may, if sates lied that no other equally efficacious remedy is provided by law (a) on the application of any person aggrieved, make an order-

(i) directing a person performing any functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do or to do that which he is required by law to do; or

(ii) declaring that any act done or proceeding taken by a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority has been done or taken without lawful authority and is of no legal effect or

(b) on the application of any person, make an, order—

(ii) requiring a person holding or purporting to hold a public office to show under what authority he claims to hold that office.

75. In the instant case, the petitioner has prayed a direction to take over possession of the Kazir Bazar Hat and also challenged the lease of the Kazir Bazar Cattle Market made by Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate. We have already held that the property in question is the property under Waqf Estate (waqfs-a-lillah) not yet acquisitioned and no compensation assessment Role was prepared no the property vested to the Government and that the Mutawalli of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate is not performing any function in connection with affairs of the republic but in the capacity of the terms of the Waqf deed of Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Md Ahia Waqf Estate (commonly known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate) and as such we do not find any ground to pass any order upon the respondent No. 6.

76. The respondent No. 1 and 2 in their affidavit-in-opposition admitted that the property relates to the property of the Waqf Estate and as such we also do not find any ground to make any direction upon the Respondents No. 1 and 2 to take any steps until and unless the property vest upon the Republic in accordance with law.

77. The allegations made in the instant writ petition as well as the affidavit-in-opposition made by the respondent No. 5 that the lease of the, cattle market is very low; in such situation we observe that under section 10A there is proviso which reads as follows :

"Provided that—

(i) No such Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee shall be entitled to transfer, or to create any encumbrance or charge on, any such interest in any khas land in any manner otherwise than by a temporary lease but no such temporary lease shall be given for a period exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the, agricultural year in which it is created, nor shall any tree be cut down or building demolished, except with the previous permission of the Collector and on such terms as the Collector may prescribe in that behalf; and any transfer or any encumbrance or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision thereof shall be null and void and the full value of any tree cut down or building demolished in such contravention shall be recoverable from the Mutawalli, Shebait or trustee, an arrear of rent or land revenue;"

78. The aforementioned provision being a mandatory one .the Mutawalli shall give temporary lease for a period not exceeding one year at a time expiring on the last day of the Agricultural year. If any lease given in contravention of such proviso the lease thereof shall be null and void and as such the Mutawalli, should give lease of the Kazir Bazar Cattle Market in accordance with law on yearly basis not exceeding one year.

79. The Rule of writ petition No. 9256 of 2005 is discharged with the above observation however without any order as to the costs.

80. The ad-interim order granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

The Rules issued in Writ Petition No. 300 of 2006, Writ Petition. No. 301 of 2006 and Writ Petition No. 331 of 2006 are disposed of however without any order as to the costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J: This Rule Nisi was issued upon an application by the petitioner under Article 102 (2) of the Constitution upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo bearing No. Bhu: Mo: Sha-7/ Bibidh-14 /2005-630 dated 19-12-2006 issued under the signature of the respondent No. 2 requesting the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to take action as per the instruction given in the said memo as evident from Annexure-G to the writ petition so far as it relates to the petitioner shall not be declared to have been made illegally and without any lawful authority and /or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that the representatives of the local community and the people of the locality by virtue of their easement right are in possession and enjoyment of Mohal Shamil Fisheries. All the petitioners were the representatives of neighbouring villages, the petitioner No. 1 was the representative of village Purnachogaon situated within Police Station Companygonj, District-Sylhet. He used to look after the fishery namely, "Puckchaoir and Furar Khal. Mohal Shamil Jolkor" measuring an area of 14.68 acres of land and accordingly the Petitioner No. 1 paid ground rent against the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor upto 1414 BS; the petitioner No. 2 was the representative of the villagers of village-Boulgra, situated under the Police Station-Companygonj, District Sylhet. He used to look after the fishery namely "Lolir Haor Mohal Shamil Jolkor" measuring an area of 3.69 acres of land and paid ground rent against the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor upto 1414 BS. The petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 were the representatives of the villagers of village Shekherkhal and Noapara, situated under the police station Goainghat, District Sylhet. The villagers nominated these two petitioners to look after the fishery namely "Manan Khal and Noapara Mohal Shami Jolkor" measuring an area of 4.56 acres of land, the petitioners also paid ground rent against the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor upto 1414 BS. The petitioner No. 5 was nominated as the representative of the village "Khajakuri, and Inchapur Mohal Khamil Jolkor" measuring an area of 5.50 acres of land and he also paid ground rent against the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor up to 1414 BS. The petitioner No. 6 was the representative of the village Angerjur situated within the police station Goainghat, District-Sylhet. The said villagers nominated the petitioner No. 6 for looking after the fishery namely "Purba Damari and Furarpar Mohal Shamil Jolkor" measuring an area of 2.97 acres of land and accordingly the petitioner No. 6 paid ground rent against the said Jolkor upto 1414 BS; the petitioner No. 7 was the representative of the villagers of village-Kandigram, situated within police station Goainghat, District-Sylhet. The said villagers nominated the said petitioner for looking after the fishery namely "Vaily Kuri Chirurkhal Mohal Shamil Jolkor" measuring an area of 1.82 acres of land and accordingly the petitioner No. 7 paid ground rent against the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor upto 1414 BS.

3. The "Mohal Shamil Fisheries" of Sylhet used to be managed by the Government from time to time by issuing circular giving right to the concerned villagers to catch fish for home consumption through the representatives of the villagers on payment of ground rent. For the first time such circular was issued on 17-7-1964 by the Board of Revenue, the then Government of East Pakistan, Dacca. Thereafter Bangladesh Government through the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms (now Ministry of Land) published a circular dated 1-8-1973 relating to lease of Government fisheries. Under clause 32 of the said circular the government instructed the field level officers how the Mohal Shamil Jolkors would be managed and settled. 

4. Subsequently, the Ministry of Land published two guidelines for regulating lease of Government fisheries but in those guidelines nowhere it has been mentioned as to how the Mohal Shamil Fisheries would be managed. 

5. In this situation the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Goainghat issued a Memo proposing certain issues relating to the management of the Mohal Shamil Fisheries. The Upazila Nirbahi Officer sent the Memo to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet on 24-1-2005. 

6. In pursuance of the said Memo the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet prepared a comprehensive report which relates to the management of the Mohal Shamil Jolkors and for-warded the same to the Secretary, Ministry of Land for a specific guideline with regard to the management of the Mohal Shamil Jolkors. 

7. After receiving the said Memo the Ministry of Land by its letter dated 5-9-2005 asked the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to send a comprehensive report relating to present position of the Mohal Shamil Jolkors so that the Ministry of Land would be in a position to make a specific guideline with regard to the said Jolkors. After receiving the letter from the government the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet vide letter dated 28-11-2005 sent a report to the Ministry stating the position of Mohal Shamil Jolkors within his District. 

8. The petitioner approached the District Administration for the payment of ground rent for the year of 1415 BS, which they refused to accept. This came as a surprise to the petitioners as the Mohal Shamil Jolkors were in fact settled in the name of the representatives of concerned villagers and accordingly SA Khatian was prepared and ground rent paid. On further inquiry the petitioners learnt that the respondent No. 1 instead of providing a guide-line for the management of the Mohal Shamil directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to take steps as per the existing fishery Settlement Policy Guideline. The latest Policy guideline provides for leasing out the fisheries by negotiation and by tender. In the said guideline nothing was said with regard to the Mohal Shamil Jolkor and no such clarification was made under the said guideline. The petitioners also learnt that the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was taking steps for leasing out the Mohal Shamil Jolkors by tender. 

9. The petitioners however, collected a copy of the order given by the Ministry. It transpires from the said order dated 19-12-2006 that the Ministry asked the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to lease out the Mohal Shamil Jalkors by tender. After coming to know about the said letter the petitioners sent a Demand of Justice Notice to the Government asking them to withdraw/rescind/cancel the said order and to allow the petitioners to catch fish in the said Mohal Shamil Jolkors. Since the respondents did not pay any heed to it the petitioner moved this Court and challenged the impugned order dated 9-12-2006 and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

10. Mr Md Motahar Hossain, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 did not file any affidavit-in-opposition, rather he candidly submits that there should be a policy guideline for the purpose of proper management of the Mohal Shamil Jolkors in the light of the national policy guideline, particularly to avoid any further complication in future. 

11. Dr AKM Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that from time immemorial the villagers had been enjoying the facilities of catching fish from the Mohal Shamil Jolkors. Now it has become a customary right of the villagers of the locality. Without considering their right the Government has issued the impugned order, as such the same is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Dr Ali further submits that Mohal Shamil Jolkor is a fishery of separate and distinct category, classified not for leasing, but for the use of local people of the community to catch fish for home consumption on payment of ground rent. As such, on payment of such rent the petitioners should be allowed to enjoy the said Mohal Shamil Jolkor as before. 12. Dr Ali further submits that the respondent No. I as per the report of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was required to provide a policy guideline as existed under the policy of 1964 and 1973 for the management of Mohal Shamil Fisheries. Unfortunately, the respondent No. 1 without providing any policy guide-line arbitrarily issued the impugned memo directing the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, to lease out the Mohal Shamil Jolkor (fisheries) in the light of existing settlement policy of the fisheries and, as such, the said memo is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority. 

13. Dr. Ali further submits, that the local Administration, particularly the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and the Deputy Commissioner, time and again requested the respondent in the Ministry of Land of the Government of Bangladesh to issue a Guideline for the better management of the Mohal Shamil Fisheries. But the respondent No.1 totally ignoring the recommendations sent from the office of the local Administration had issued the impugned order without considering the long standing customary right of the local people of, inter alia Jaintapur, Goainghat and Kanaighat Police Stations. 

14. Dr. Ali further submits that in the past the Mohal Shamil Fisheries were never leased out to anyone. This unique practice within Jaintapur Porgona (Now Jaintapur Upazila and two other Upazilas) is one of its kind in Bangladesh giving a right to the villagers of that locality to catch fish from such Mohal Shamil Jolkor for home consumption on payment of ground rent only. As such the petitioners should be allowed to continue to pay such ground rent as before and enjoy the Mohal Shamil Fisheries. He submits that the impugned direction of the respondent No. 1 is in conflict with the established right of the petitioner's and, as such, the impugned direction of the Government as contained in Annexure-G to the writ petition is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

15. Dr. Ali further submits that although there were two policy Guidelines published in past in the year 1991 and 2005 with regard to management of fisheries of the country, and in the year 2009 new policy guideline was also published but in these three policy guidelines the fisheries popularly known as Mohal Shamil Jolkor was not given any place or importance. Thus, no policy exists with regard to how the said Jolkors of Sylhet District would be managed. Dr. Ali points out that in the year 1964, the then East Pakistan Government considering the unique nature and position of the Mohal Shamil Joklors under the District of Sylhet kept the provision to settle those Jolkors with the villagers representatives. Similar view was also taken by the government vide circular dated 1-8-1973 after the Liberation of the country. He submits that after 1973 the respondents in the Ministry of Land totally failed to consider this aspect. All of a sudden they issued the impugned order without assessing the rights which had been enjoyed by the local people in the said Mohal Shamil Jolkors from time immemorial. As such the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

16. We have gone through the writ petition along with the annexures. We have also considered the submission made by the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the respondents. The Mohal Sharnil Jalkor is a kind of fishery in which villagers catch fish collectively/individually for their home consumption. This Mohal Shamil Jolkars have a long tradition. Catching fish in the said Jalkor is a very old custom of the people of Jainta Porgona under the District of Sylhet. Before 1835, there was a Porgona namely, Jaintapur in short Jainta Pargona, which was an independent kingdom till 1835. After 1835 it became the part of British Raj and became part of Sylhet District. At that time Sylhet had two divisions, one was Jainta Porgona and the rest of the district was known as Moghlan. Jainta Porgona comprised of 17 Porgonas covering an area of 483/484 square miles or 3,10,000 acres. They were situated in the north-east corner of the district and with the exception of Porgonas at bank lay between the Surma River and the Khashi and Jainta Hills. They originally formed part of the territories of the Jainta Raja. Hundreds of years back the present Jaintapur Police Station, Kanaighat Police Station and Goainghat Police Station were the part of Jainta Porgana. The Mohal Shamil Jolkors are situated within these three police stations, earlier which were under the former Jainta Porgona of Jainta Raja. 

17. "The land being very low-lying the Jainta Parganas were rich in fisheries and for many years these have been divided into two classes, the larger and more accessible being sold by auction to the highest bidder for a year or a short period of years, and the smaller and more remote fisheries being settled as village fisheries with certain persons of the neighbouring villages as representatives of all the inhabitants. The latter fisheries were known as Mohal Shamil Jolkar and the lease was intended to be rather a licence to fish than a lease. The revenue was fixed at a low rate at each resettlement, and the licence contained clauses restricting the payment to be demanded for use of the fishery from neighbouring villagers, and forbidding subletting by auction sale or otherwise. 

18. The total number of Mohal Shamil Fisheries, when Mr WL Scott's Survey took place in 1914-18, was 428. Of these, ten (10) ceased to be Mohal Shamil Fisheries as a result of decision by Civil Courts. Out of the remaining 418 fisheries, 179 (Goainghat PS 105, Kanaighat PS 44 and Jaintiapur PS 30) were taken over by the government in 1957 and settled by auction. The fisheries which remained as Mohal Shamil Jolkars (fisheries) are 239 in number and were, later on, entrusted to Union Councils to be managed for the benefit of the local people. 

(Bangladesh District Gazette, Sylhet Chapter XII page-348). 

19. From the above it appears that the Kanaighat, Goainghat and Jaintiapur Police Stations were part of the Jaintia Parganas. The Mohal Shamil Jolkors were under the control of the Jaintia Raja. During the rule of "Raja" the villagers used to enjoy the right to catch fish for their home consumption on payment of very low rent.

20. We find from Annexure-'B' that the government of East Pakistan in the year 1964 issued a Government Order with the subject: "Management and settlement of the Government fisheries." 

21. This Government order was issued vide Memo 700/ (2)-2 SM (122)/63 Dacca 17-7-1964. By this order the Government decided to resettle the Mohal Shamil Fisheries with the villagers representatives. The provision mentioned in clause 4 of the said Government order runs as follows: 

"There were 423 Mohal Shamil fisheries in Jainta Parganas of Sylhet district, of those, 175 bigger ones which developed into valuable fisheries, were brought on the list of regular fisheries and are being leased by Government in the normal way. The GO (Government order) does not cover these 175 fisheries which are no longer Mohal Shamil fisheries. The Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet may, therefore, prepare their resettlement with the village representatives and initiate proposals through the divisional Commissioner." 

22. Thereafter in the year 1973 after the Liberation War of Bangladesh the Government issued another Government order G.O. vide Memo No. 1/M/38 JM(Dacca), 1-8-1977. The subject of the said Memo was: 

"Revised principles of lease of Government fisheries." 

23. The contents of the provision made in paragraph 32 of the government order dated 1-8-1977 runs as follows: 

"32. Mohal Shamil Fisheries in the Jaintia Porganas of Sylhet district, wherein the villagers used to catch fish for home consumption, shall continue to be settled with the representatives of people of only those villages on payment of ground rent as before, until further orders." 

24. It appears that the Government positively considered the custom and long usage which prevailed regarding Mohal Shamil Fisheries of Sylhet district and giving importance to the customary right of the villagers of the locality of Jaintapur, Kanaighat and Goainghat police station, (Upazillas). The government took the decision to allow the villagers to catch fish for their home consumption from the Mohal Shamil Fisheries. 

25. In the year, 1991 the Government for the First time, adopted সরকারী জলমহল, বালু মহল ও পাথর মহল নীতিমাল। in the said Nitimala nothing has been mentioned regarding the management of Mohal Shamil Jolkor. Facing the difficulties to manage the Mohal Shamil Jolkors situated under Goainghat, Kanaighat and Jaintiapur Upazila, under District Sylhet, the Field Officers sent some recommendations to the Government suggesting how to manage Mohal Shamil Jolkors. The Upazila Nirbahi Officer Goainghat vide Memo উনিঅকো/গোঃঘাট/২০০৫/৮৫/১(৫) তাং ২৪-১-২০০৫ (Annexure-C) sent a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet giving a copy to the Secretary, Local Government, Rural Development, Commissioner, Sylhet Division, Zonal Settlement Officer, Sylhet and Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Sylhet. In that letter the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, gave some suggestions how to manage the Mohal Shamil Jalkor /Fisheries. The suggestions given by the UNO Goinghat is given hereunder—

গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার
উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসারের কার্যালয়
গোয়াইনঘাট, সিলেট।
স্বারক নং উনি অকা/গোঃঘাট/২০০৫

বিষয়ঃ গোয়াইনঘাট উপজেলাধীন “মহাল শামিল” জলমহাল গুলির ব্যবস্থাপনা প্রসংগে।

উপর্যুক্ত বিষয়ে মহোদয়ের সদয় দৃষ্টি আকর্ষন পূর্বক জানাচ্ছি যে, সিলেট জেলার গোয়াইঘাট উপজেলাসহ পার্শ্ববর্তী আরো 

 

কয়েকটি উপজেলার “মহাল শামিল” নামে এক ধরণের জলমহালের অস্তিত্ব রয়েছে। গোয়াইনঘাট উপজেলায় বিভিন্ন আয়তনের সর্বমোট “মহাল শামিল” জলমহাল আছে। এসএ রেকর্ডে উক্ত মহাল শামিল গুলি দোবারা রেকর্ড হয়েছে। প্রাথমিকভাবে মহাল শামিলগুলি ১ নং খাস, খাতিয়ানে রেকর্ডভূক্ত হলেও প্রত্যেকটি মৌজার সংশ্লিষ্ট মহাল শামীল এর দাগগুলি নিয়ে অপর একটি পৃথক খতিয়ান খুলে দোবারাভাবে “সরপঞ্জের প্রধান” নামে রেকর্ডভূক্ত করা হয়েছে। চলমান আর এস, জরিপে উক্ত মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলি ১ নং খতিয়ানে এবং এসএ রেকর্ডের অনুরূপ দোবারাভাবে কোনকোন ক্ষেত্রে “.......মহাল শামীল..........গ্র্যাম্য জনসাধারনের পক্ষে.......নং সার্কেলের সরপঞ্জ” উখিয়া “.......... মৌজার. .........গ্রামের জনসাধারণের পক্ষে” অথবা”............গ্রাম বাসীর পক্ষে...... (এক/একাধিক) ব্যক্তি হিসাবে” রেকর্ড প্রচারিত হয়েছে।


০২। উক্ত মহাল শামিল গুলির ব্যবস্থাপনা বিষয়ে কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট নীতমালা না থাকার চলমান আর,এস, জরীপে সরকার পক্ষ থেকে যথাযথভাবে প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করার ক্ষেত্রে সমস্যা সৃষ্টি হচ্ছে। সেটেলমেন্ট বিভাগ এস,এ রেকর্ডে বর্ণিত “সরপঞ্জের প্রধান” শব্দটির পরিবর্তে পূর্ব বর্ণিত শব্দ/বাক্যগুলি কিসের ভিত্তিতে বা কোন আইনের আওতায় প্রতিস্থাপন করেছে তা বোধ-গম্য নয়। মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলির মালিকানার কলামে ভিন্ন ভিন্ন অভিব্যক্তি প্রতিস্থাপন হওয়ায় উক্ত জলমহালগুলির মালিকানা নিয়ে অনিশ্চয়তা দেয়া দিয়েছে।

০৩ । স্থানীয় গণ্যমান্য ব্যক্তিবর্গের সংগে আলোচনায় জানা যায় যে, দীর্ঘদিন যাবৎ উক্ত মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলি পাশ্ববর্তী গ্রামবাসী প্রথাগতভাবে ভোগদখল করে আসছে। স্থানীয় জনসাধারণ উক্ত জলমহাল হতে বর্ষাকালে মৎস্য আহরণ করেন, শুল্ক মৌসুমে তারা গরু চরানো সহ অন্যান্য প্রথাগত অধিকার প্রয়োগ করে আসছেন ।

০৪। পূর্ব বর্ণিত মহাল শামিল বিষয়ে ১-৮-১৯৭৩ তারিখের তৎকালীন ভূমি প্রশাসন ও সংস্কার মন্ত্রণালয়ের স্মারক নং ঃ ১ম-৩৭৩/৭৩/১২১৯৩৮) জে এম এর ৩২ নং অনুচ্ছেদে বর্ণনা করা হয় যে, “সিলেট জেলার জয়ন্তিয়া পরগণার মহাল শামিল জনমহালগুলি যেখানে গ্রামবাসীর নিজেদের পরিবারের আহারের জন্য মাছ ধরিয়া আসিতেছে সেগুলি পৃনরাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যস্ত দেওয়ার শর্তে বন্দোবস্ত দেওয়া চলিতে থাকিবে ।” পরবতীতে এ বিষয়ে কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট দিক নির্দেশনা পাওয়া যায় নি।

কিন্তু সাম্প্রতিক সময়ে অত্র উপজেলায় কিছু কিছু মহাল শামিল সরেজমিনে তদন্ত করে দেখা যায় যে, কয়েকটি মহাল শামিল বর্তমানে সম্পূর্ণ/আংশিকভাবে ভরাট হয়েছে । মহাল শামিল গুলিতে মৎস্য আহরণের যে প্রথাগত অধিকার ০১/০৯/১৯৭৩ তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপনে প্রদান করা হয়েছিল, উক্ত জলমহালগুলি ভরাট হয়ে গেলে এবং তাতে মৎস্য আহরণ বন্ধ হয়ে গেলে প্রথাগত অধিকারের বিলুপ্তি ঘটার কথা । শ্রেণী পরিবর্তনের পর উক্ত মহাল শামিলগুলির সংশিষ্ট জমির ব্যবস্থাপনা কি হবে সে বিষয়ে কোন দিক নির্দেশনা নাই। শ্রেণী পরিবর্তিত হয়ে ভরাট হলে উক্ত মহাল শামিলগুলি বেদখল হাবার ব্যাপক সম্ভানা হয়েছে।

০৫। গোয়াইনঘাট উপজেলার মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলি স্থানীয় গ্রামবাসীর পক্ষে কেহ কেহ খাজনা (ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর) পরিশোধ করে ভোগদখল করে আসছেন । কিন্তু গ্রামবাসীর পক্ষে কে গ্রামবাসীর প্রকৃত প্রতিনিধিত্ব করে তা নির্ধারণ করার কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট সংজ্ঞা নাই । এস,এ রেকর্ডে বর্ণিত “সরপঞ্জ” নামক কোন স্থানীয়/সরকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান বাংলাদেশের আইনে নাই ফলে স্থানীয় মাতবর বা প্রভাবশালী শ্রেণীর কোন ব্যক্তি গ্রামবাসীর পক্ষে ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর পরিশোধ করে ভোগদখল করে । কিন্তু ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর পরিশোধ করার জন্য কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তি/প্রতিষ্ঠানের কোন সুনিনিষ্ট দায়দাযিত্/দায়বদ্ধতা না থাকার কারণে অনেক ক্ষেত্রে ভূমি উন্নয়ন করা বকেয়া থেকে যায়। কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তি/প্রতিষ্ঠান উক্ত মহাল শামিলের দায়িত্বে না থাকায় বকেয়া ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর (খাজনা) আদায়ে বিন সৃষ্টি হয়। এভাবে বিপুল পরিমাণ ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর বকেয়া রয়েছে।

০৬। পূর্ব বর্ণিত মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলির প্রকৃত মালিকানা কার/কাদের নামে নির্ধারণ করা হবে এ বিষয়ে ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের সুনির্দিষ্ট দিক নির্দেশনা/নীতিমালার প্রযোজন । যদিও দীর্ঘ কাল যাবৎ গ্রামবাসীগণ উক্ত জলমাহালগুলিতে তাদের প্রথাগত অধিকার প্রয়োগ করেছেন তাই তাৎক্ষনিকভাবে তাদের প্রথাগত অধিকার বন্ধ করা হল তারা বিজ্ঞ আদালতের আশ্রয় গ্রহন করবেন। কিন্তু ব্যবস্তাপনার সুবিধার্থে এসএ রেকর্ডে বর্ণিত“সরপঞ্জ” বা চলমান আর, এস, জরিপে বর্ণিত “গ্রামবাসীদের পক্ষে” অভিব্যক্তির প্রকৃতপক্ষে কে বা কোন আইনগত/বিধিবদ্ধ প্রতিষ্ঠান প্রতিনিধিত করবে তা সুনির্দিষ্ট ভাবে নির্ধারণ করা উচিত। প্রচলিত আইনের আলোকে স্থানীয় ইউনিয়ন পরিষদের নির্বাচিত মেম্বার বা মহিলা মেম্বারকে পদাধিকার বলে উক্ত“সরপঞ্জের” প্রতিস্থাপন হিসাবে গণ্য করে/বিধি চালু করা যায়।

০৭। প���রচলিত নিয়মে গ্রামবাসীদের পক্ষে কোন স্থানীয় প্রভাবশালী ব্যক্তি ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর (খাজনা) পরিশোধ করে উক্ত জলমহালের মাছ মৎস্য শিকার মৌসুমে বিক্রি করে কিছু অর্থ গ্রামবাসীদের মধ্যে বিতরণ করে, কিছু অর্থ স্থানীয় শিক্ষা/ধর্মীয় প্রতিষ্ঠানের উন্নয়নের কাজে ব্যবহার করে। কিন্তু কোন সুনিদিষ্ট দায়বদ্ধতা না থাকায় উক্ত অর্থ বেশীরভাগ ক্ষেত্রে যথাযথভাবে ব্যবহার হয় না। আবার এভাবে মংস্য বিক্রি করা অর্থ ভাগাভাগি করে নেওয়া পূর্ব বর্ণিত ১-৮-১৯৭৩ তারিখের জারীকৃত নীতিমালার পরিপন্থী ।

০৮ ।তাই সার্বিক পর্যালোচনায় গোয়াইনঘাট উপজেলার মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলির ক্ষেত্রে নিম্ন বর্ণিত দিক নির্দেশনা কামনা করা হলোঃ-

(ক) চলমান আর, এস জরিপে পূর্ব বর্ণিত মহাল শামিল জলমহালগুলি কার নামে (অর্থাৎ মালিকানা) কিভাবে রেকর্ড হবে সে বিষয়ে ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের নির্দেশনা গ্রহণ। কোন নির্দেশনা ছাড়াই আর, এস রেকর্ডে পূর্ব বর্ণিত মালিকানাকে কিসের ভিত্তিতে পরিবর্তন করা হলো সে বিষয়ে জোনাল সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসারের নিকট পত্র প্রেরণ করা যায়।

(খ) মহাল শামিলগুলির ব্যবস্তাপনার ক্ষেত্রে কোন সুনির্দিষ্ট নীতিমালা/সার্কুলার জারী করার জন্য ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করা যায়।

(গ) এস এ রেকর্ডে বা চলমান আর, এস জরিপে মহাল শামিল গুলির মালিকানার বিষয়ে পূর্ব বর্ণিত অভিব্যক্তির ক্ষেত্রে স্থানীয় ইউনিয়ন পরিষদকে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করে বিধি প্রণয়ন করার জন্য ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষন করা যায়। এছাড়া, উক্ত মহাল শামিলগুলির ক্ষেত্রে ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর (খাজনা) কি হারে নির্ধারিত হবে সে বিষযে সুনির্দিষ্ট দিক নির্দেশনা চেয়ে ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ে পত্র প্রেরণ করা যায়।

(ঘ) মহালশামিলগুলি ভরাট হয়ে শ্রেণী পরিবর্তিত হলে উক্ত পরিবর্তিত শ্রেণীর জমির ব্যবস্থাপনা কি হবে সে বিষয়ে ভুমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের নির্দেশ কামনা করা যায়।

বিষয়ঃ সিলেট জেলার বিভিন্ন উপজেলায় অবস্থিত মহাল শামিল জলকর ব্যবস্থাপনার লক্ষ্যে সুনির্দিষ্ট নীতিমালা প্রনয়ন প্রসঙ্গে ।

উল্লেখিত বিষয়ের প্রেক্ষিতে অবগতির জন্য জানানো যাচ্ছে, সিলেট জেলায় তৎকালীন জৈন্তা পরগনায় মোট ৪২৩টি মহাল সামিল জলকরের অস্তিত্ব ছিল। এই জলমহালগুলো তৎকালীন আইনে প্রথাগত অধিকারের ভিত্তিতে স্থানীয় জনসাধারণের কর্তৃক যৎসামান্য খাজনা পরিশোধের মাধ্যমে ভোগ দখল করা হতো ।

০২। নথিপত্র পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় এই ৪২০ টি মহাল সামিল জলকরের মধ্যে ১৭৫ টি মহাল শামিল জলকর অধুনালুপ্ত ইষ্ট পাকিস্থান বোর্ড অব রেভিনিউ কর্তৃক অধিযাচনের মাধ্যমে নিয়মিত জলমহালের তালিকায় আনা হয় এবং সেগুলো বর্তমানে নিয়মিত জলমহাল হিসেবে ইজারা প্রদান করা হচ্ছে। পরবর্তীতে অবশিষ্ট ২৪৮ টি জলকর ব্যবস্থাপনা সম্পর্কে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করা হয়নি।

০৩। বিগত ১৯৭৩ ইং সনে ১/৮/১৯৭৩ ইং তারিখে ভূমি প্রশাসন ভূমি সংস্কার মন্ত্রণালয় কর্তৃক জারীকৃত ১ম ১৭৩/৭৩/১২১৯(৩৮) জে, এল নং স্মারক পত্রের ৩২ নং অনুচ্ছেদের সিলেট জেলার জৈন্তা পরগণার মহাল শামিল জলকর গুলো যেখানে যে অবস্থায় আছে পুরনাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত গ্রামবাসীদের নিয়ন্ত্রনে থাকবে বলে বর্ণিত হয়েছে । পরবর্তীতে এ বিষয়ে আর কোন দিক নির্দেশনা প্রদান করা হয়নি ।

০৪ ।গত ১৯৯১ ইং সনে প্রণীত জলমহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা ও নীতিমালা ও মহাল শামিল জলকার ব্যবস্থাপনা সম্পকে দিক নির্দেশনা প্রদান করা হয়নি। সংগত কারণে এই মহাল সামিল জলকরগুলোর সুষ্ঠু ব্যবস্তাপনায় যথেষ্ট ব্যত্যয় সৃষ্টি হচ্ছে।

০৫। সম্প্রতি উপজেলা নির্বাহী অফিসার গোয়াইনঘাট হতে একটি বিশদ প্রতিবেদন পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় (কপি সংযুক্ত) সরেজমিন পরিদর্শনকালে কিছু কিছু মহাল শামিল জলকর সম্পূর্ণ ভরাট হয়ে অস্তিতৃবিলুপ্তির পথে এবং কিছু কিছু মহাল আংশিক ভরাট হয়ে মৎস্য আহরণের অনুপোযোগী হয়ে পড়েছে। এই মহাল শামিল জলকরগুলো যদি শুকিয়ে যায় তাহলে স্থানীয় জনসাধারণের প্রথাগত অধিকার বিলুপ্ত হওয়ার কথা । কিন্তু সুনির্দিষ্ট কোন নীতিমালা না থাকায় এ বিষয়ে বাস্তব সম্মত কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করা সম্ভব হচ্ছে না। সময় উপযোগী কোন ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা না হলে মহাল সামিল জলকরের ভূমি বেদখল হয়ে যাওয়ার সন্তাবনা বিদ্যমান |

০৬। এ বিষয়ে যে সকল মহাল শামিল জলকর গুলো শুকিয়ে গিয়েছে শ্রেণী পরিবর্তন করে কৃষি খাস হিসেবে ভূমিহীনদের মধ্যে বন্দোবস্ত প্রদান এবং এখন যে সকল জলমহাল হতে মৎস্য আহরণ উপযোগী রয়েছে সেগুলির ব্যবস্থাপনা উপজেলা প্রশাসনের হাতে অর্পন করা হলে একাদিক যেমন সরকারী স্বার্থ রক্ষিত হবে, তেমনি ভূমিহীন জনগোষ্ঠী ও উপকৃত হবে।

27. After sending this report the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was asked to send details of Mohal Shamil Jolkors. After receiving the letter from the respondent No. 1, by his letter dated 28-11-2005, Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet specifically requested the respondent No. 1 to adopt a specific guideline for management of total 203 Mohal Shamil Jokors out of which 40 situated in Jaintapur, 133 in Gohainghat and 30 Jolkors in Kanaighat Upazila under the District Sylhet. 

28. It is to be noted that as per report of Mr. WL Scott there were 428 Jolkors, in 1914-18. Out of those, Government took over 179 fisheries in 1957. Thereafter 239 Jolkors remained as Mohal Shamil. Many of the Jolkors being silted up presently there are only 203 Jolkors are remaining as Mohal Shamil. 

29. But it appears from the record that the national policy guideline for management of fisheries for the year 2005 was adopted on 20-12-2005, which was published by Gazette Notification on 15-1-2006. But unfortunately the recommendation and suggestion of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and the Upazila Nirbahi Officer Goainghat regarding Mohal Shamil Fisheries were totally ignored in this policy guideline. The Government did not mention anything in respect of Mohal Shamil Jolkors of Sylhet District. 

30. Dr Ali informed us that another policy guideline was adopted in the year 2009, although it has not been annexed with this Writ Petition, but Dr Ali informed us that in the said policy guideline also there nothing regarding the management of the Mohal Shamil Jolkor. 

31. It appears that when the petitioners were expecting a specific guideline for the Mohal Shamil Fisheries as suggested by the Deputy Commissioner and Upazila Nirbahi Officers. The respondent No. 1, all of a sudden, issued the impugned letter by which the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was asked to give lease of those fisheries by tender. In the order it has been said that the fisheries, whose area is more than 20 acres would be settled by the District জলমহল ব্যবস্থাপনা কমিটি; the fisheries less than 20 acres and more than three acres in area would be settled by the Upazila Committee and the remaining Jalmohals of Mohal Shamil Jolkor, which are less than 3 acres in area would be settled with the villagers for their use by the respective Union Parishad. It appears that the fisheries which were more than 20 acres and the fisheries which were less than 20 acres but more than 3 acres would be given by way of lease by open tender, and only the remaining fisheries, which were under three acres would be settled by the Union Parishad with the villagers. It also appears that in the order it was stated that the Jolkors which were already silted up would be managed as per Nitimala. 

32. From the age old history of Sylhet district it appears that the existence of Mohal Shamil Jolkors were only in Jaintia Pargana which subsequently came under the District of Sylhet. Other this district the existence of this find of Jolkor is absent throughout the country. We have already gone through the extract of the report of WL Scott printed in Bangladesh District Gazetteer Sylhet, Ch-XII, page 348. In this report it was mentioned that 348 Mohal Shamil Jolkors used to be settled and resettled with the villagers as long back in 1914, probably it extended before that time. Since Jaintiapur (Jainta Pargana) in the year 1835 came under the control of Sylhet District, it may be presumed that there was existence of Mohal Shamil Jolkor at least during 1835. 

33. From the History of Sylhet published in Bangladesh District Gazetteer (in Chapter-II page-47 last paragraph) it further appears that during Mughal occupation of Sylhet in 1612 the Independence of Jainta Raja was not affected. Presumably it can be said that the "Raiyat" of Raja enjoyed the right to catch fish from the Mohal Shamil Jolkors during that time also. The people of previous Jainta Pargona had enjoyed this right till 1414 BS as of custom and customary right. 

34. Now let us see what is custom, customary law and customary right. 

35. In the book “আইন শব্দ কোষ” compiled and edited by Mr Justice Mohammad Habibur Rahman the former Chief Justice of Bangladesh and Mr Anisuzzaman Professor Emeritus Dhaka University, the meaning of Custom and customary law is defined as under:

"custom n. প্রথা বি. যে-রীতি কোনো বিশেষ এলাকায় এমনভাবে অনুসৃত হয় যে, উহাকে ওই এলাকার আইনের অংশস্বরুপ গ্রহন করিতে প্রথাগত আইন হিসাবে স্বীকৃত হইতে হইলে ইহাকে যুক্তিসংগত প্রকৃতির হইতে হয় এবং ইহা স্মরণাতীত কাল হইতে নিরবিচ্ছিন্নভাবে অধিকার হিসাবে অনুসৃত হইতে হয় বাংলাদেশের সংবিধানের ১৫২(১) অনুচ্ছেদে প্রথাকেও আইন হিসাবে গণ্য করা হইয়াছে।

Customary law প্রথাগত আইন যে-আইন আইনগত শর্ত বা অবশ্যপালনীয় আচরণ-বিধি হিসাবে গৃহীত রীতিনীতির সমন্বয়ে গঠিত। যে-সকল লোক-ব্যবহার একটি সামাজিক ও অর্থনৈতিক ব্যবস্থার এতই সারভুত ও সাংসিদ্ধিক অংশ যে ওইগুলি আইন বলিয়া গণ্য করা হয়।”

36. Customary right was saved under clause 2 (b) of the Easement Act 1882. The pro-vision of this clause runs as follows: 

2. Nothing herein contained shall be deemed to affect any law not hereby expressly repealed; or to derogate from 
(a)  ...........
(b) any customary or other right (not being a license) in or over immovable property which the government, the public or any person may possess irrespective of other immovable property; 

In defining customary right, in the case of Raj Nandan Singh vs Ram Kishun Lohar, reported in AIR 1958 Patna at Page 571 their Lordship held that—

"A customary right no doubt exists, independent of any dominant heritage and is vested in a defined class or community of a particular locality, as distinguished from individuals for their sole benefit." 

37. In distinguishing scope of customary rights from customary easement their Lord-ships in the case of Parbhawati Devi vs Mahendra Singh reported in AIR 1981 Patna 133 held that "the customary rights arise by custom, but unappurtenant to a dominant tenement. No fixed period of enjoyment is necessary to establish these rights, but the custom must be reasonable and certain. 

38. In the case of Ram Chandra Shah vs Abdul Handan AIR 1984 Patna 313 their Lordships held that—

"Easements are Private rights belonging to particular persons wile customary rights are public right annexed to the place in general." 

39. In the case of Raghova vs Anandabai reported in AIR 1930 Nag 40 it was held that a customary right can be acquired only in favour of a class or community. The Privy Council in the case of Lakshinder Misra vs Rangalal, AIR 1950 PC 56 observed that—

"A customary right can exist only in relation to the inhabitants of a district and it cannot be claimed in respect of the public at large. The Custom, if established makes the local law of the district and it creates a right in each of inhabitants irrespective of his estate or interest in any particular property." 

40. From the facts of the case in our hand, we are of the view that the villagers of former Jainta Porgona possess a right by custom. Considering this right the then Government of East Pakistan kept the provision to settle these kind of Jolkors with the local villagers. Even after the Liberation of Bangladesh the Government of the newborn country also admitted the existence of Mohal Shamil Jolkors. Showing respect to the customary right of the people of the then Jainta Porgona the government kept the provisions of settlement of Mohal Shamil Fisheries with the local people of Jaintapur through the representatives of the local villagers. But unfortunately subsequent Governments totally ignored the customary rights of the people of the locality which was reflected in the National Policy Guideline for the fisheries 1991 and 2005, where nothing was mentioned, how to manage the Mohal Shamil Jolkors. The Field Officers who faced difficulties in respect of management of the Mohal Shamil Jolkor, time and again requested the Government to formulate a policy guideline but we have already observed that the Government did not do so.

41. The 'custom' and 'usage' we find has been recognized as "law" under the Provision of Article 152(1) of the Constitution. The impugned order has been issued totally ignoring the customary right of the local people, in other words without considering the provision of Article 152(1) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

42. There should not be any doubt that after the partition of Pakistan when Sylhet became a part of the then East Pakistan, all the fisheries including Mohal Shamil Jolkors came under the ownership and control of the then East Pakistan Government, at present Bangladesh Government. From the memo dated 17-7-1964 (Annexure-B) it appears that 175 fisheries were enlisted as big fisheries by the then Government of East Pakistan for lease after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into force. The people of former Jainta Porgona could have challenged the inclusion of 175 fisheries in the government lists as their right to catch fish as of customary right was infringed by that inclusion. Since the people of the locality accepted the government decision of would not be wise to open a new debate on that issue. 

43. In the remaining Jolkors, the villagers including the petitioners enjoy their right to catch fish on payment of ground rent to the government, which indicates the Mohal Shamil Jolkors are also owned by the Government. The petitioners and other villagers only have the right to catch fish for their home consumption and not for commercial purpose. 

44. Considering the above facts we are of the view that for proper management of 203 Mohal Shamil Jolkors (Fisheries), which were identified by the Deputy Commissioner Sylhet vide Annexure-F, a separate policy guideline should be adopted by the Government taking into consideration the customary right and long standing usage of the local people of Jainta, Goainghat and Kanaighat Upazilas (former Jaintia Pargana) of Sylhet. 

45. The Jokors which have already been silted up have already lost their character as Jolkar, and the others which are likely to be silted up in the near further would lose their character of Jolkor very soon. For these reasons a proper guideline would also be necessary to be formulated by the Government for proper utilization of the land thus evolved from the Mohal Shamil Jolkors. 

46. We hold the view that in formulating policy guideline the respondents would keep it in their mind that since there is no existence of "Shar Pancha" in our country, (existence of which was found in Jainta Parganal ) the fisheries of the Mohal Shamil Jolkor should be settled with the elected representatives of the Union Parishad so that through them the villagers can get the benefit of the government policy. 

47. The Jolkors which have already been silted up and others upon being silted up in the future would become cultivable land and would no longer be classified as Mohal Shamil Jolkor. This kind of land is always owned by the Government like the Jolkors. The local people of the aforesaid Upazilas have a right to catch fish for home consumption only from the Mohal Shamil Jolkors as of their customary rights. On the other hand, the landless people of that locality have also a right to get settlement of land. Therefore, we are inclined to hold that at the time of formulating the policy for settling the land evolved from the Jolkors, the government would certainty give highest priority to the landless people of the neighouring areas of the land. 

48. Considering the historical background of Mohal Shamil Jolkor of Jaintia Porgana and the facts of the case we find that, at least since 1835 people of the locality of the then Jainta Porgona had been enjoying their right to catch fish from the Mohal Shamil Jolkors, which right was given by the then Jainta Raja even before 1835. In the light of the decisions mentioned above we hold that by long lapse of time this right became a customary right of the local people of Jaintapur, Goainghat and Kanaighat. The right of the people of former Jainta Porgona is an age old right, for a certain purpose, that is to catch fish from the Mohal Shamil Jolkor, and this right was restricted to the people of Jaintiapur, Goainghat and Kanaighat Upazilas only, who are a particular community. By any kind of test the right enjoyed by the people of above mentioned three Upazilas succeeded to establish the said right, as a customary right. The Government must protect this kind of right for any section of people of any area of the country irrespective of cast, creed and culture. 

49. In the light of above observation we would direct the respondents to adopt a sepa-rate policy guideline for the Mohal Shamil Jolkors considering the customary right of the local people of former Jaintia Porgona (Jaintiapur, Kanaighat and Goainghat) of Sylhet District, as soon as possible. 

50. We also hold that till a separate policy guideline of the Mohal Shamil Jolkor is adopted/formulated by the Government, the Mohal Shamil Jolkors situated within Upazila Jaintapur, Kanaighat, Goainghat or in any other area of the District would be settled with the representatives of the villagers as it was in the past. 

51. From the above discussions, we are of the view that the impugned order dated 19-12-2006 was issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

52. We find substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute with the above observations and direction. 

There would be no order as to cost. 

Let this judgment be communicated to the Secretary, Ministry of Land and all other respondents for taking necessary steps. 

End.
